On 26 January, Pistorius, the German minister of defense, stated that the tanks would be delivered in late March or early April.{{cite news|title=Deadly Russian missiles hit Ukraine power facilities|url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230126-deadly-russian-missiles-hit-ukraine-power-facilities|access-date=2023-01-26|work=France 24|date=2023-01-26}} On 24 February 2023, the German Department of Defence confirmed Germany would increase its Leopard 2A6 contribution from 14 to 18, thus providing 1 full tank battalion together with the contributions of Portugal and Sweden.{{cite tweet|author=Verteidigungsministerium|author-link=|user=Verteidigungsministerium|number=1629136976505892865|date=2023-02-24|title=Germany to provide 4 additional Leopard 2A6|language=en|access-date=2023-02-24|link=https://twitter.com/BMVg_Bundeswehr/status/1629136976505892865?s=20|quote='Verteidigungsminister Pistorius hat entschieden, weitere vier #Kampfpanzer #Leopard2 A6 aus Beständen der Bundeswehr an die #Ukraine abzugeben. Damit erhöht 🇩🇪 die Anzahl der gelieferten Panzer von 14 auf 18 & stellt zusammen mit 🇵🇹 & 🇸🇪 insgesamt ein 🇺🇦 Bataillon zur Verfügung.'|ref=}} On 27 March 2023, Germany delivered 18 Leopard 2A6 tanks to Ukraine with two accompanying armoured recovery vehicles and necessary spare parts.{{cite news|last1=Pitel|first1=Laura|title=First German Leopard 2 tanks delivered to Ukraine|url=https://www.ft.com/content/2f3f301d-8de7-426a-94fa-8bb398ffe232|access-date=2023-03-27|work=Financial Times|date=2023-03-27}} On 28 March 2023, the security board of the [[National Council (Switzerland)|Swiss National Council]] recommended that 25 Leopard 2 in storage should be sold to the German manufacturer Krauss-Maffei-Wegmann so that Germany can replace some of its own tanks now serving in Ukraine. As of this day, Switzerland keeps 96 Leopard 2 in storage. As the tanks' sale requires [[Decommission (ship)|decommissioning]], the Bundeswehr waits for approval by the Swiss parliament.{{cite news|title=Kehrtwende: Deutschland soll 25 Panzer kaufen dürfen|url=https://www.srf.ch/news/schweiz/kriegsmaterial-fuer-die-ukraine-kehrtwende-deutschland-soll-25-panzer-kaufen-duerfen|date=2023-03-27|access-date=2023-04-02|publisher=Swiss Radio and Television SRF|language=de}} On 27 September 2023, the Swiss parliament has voted to decommission 25 Leopard 2 tanks, allowing them to be sold back to Germany. Germany has given assurances that ex-Swiss tanks will not be sent to Ukraine.{{cite news|author=John Revill|date=2023-09-27|title=Swiss to sell back Leopard II tanks to help restock after Ukraine donations|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/swiss-sell-back-leopard-ii-tanks-help-restock-after-ukraine-donations-2023-09-27/|access-date=2023-09-27}} =====Poland===== Poland welcomed the German decision to allow the transfer of Leopard 2 tanks to Ukraine, with the Polish government announcing on 25 January it would transfer 14 Leopards to Ukraine from a total Polish stock of 247, in addition to a further 50–60 Soviet-era tanks.{{cite news|last1=Easton|first1=Andrew|title=Poland says it is ready to send 14 Leopard tanks to Ukraine|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/live/world-europe-64396659?pinned_post_locator=urn:asset:91846f35-da18-45f4-a960-7d18b6acfa59|access-date=2023-01-25|work=BBC News|date=2023-01-25}} On 24 February 2023, the first 4 Leopard 2A4 tanks from Polish stocks were delivered to Ukraine. These are the first Leopard 2 tanks to be operated by Ukraine.{{cite news|title=Poland delivers first Leopard tanks to Ukraine – DW – 02/24/2023|url=https://www.dw.com/en/poland-delivers-first-leopard-tanks-to-ukraine/a-64809432|access-date=2023-02-24|work=DW|date=2023-02-24|language=en}} =====Canada===== On 26 January 2023, the Canadian [[Minister of National Defence (Canada)|Defence Minister]], [[Anita Anand]], announced that Canada would be sending four Leopard 2A4 tanks to Ukraine, with the potential for more to follow. These vehicles were reportedly 'combat ready.' Canada will also provide appropriate training to Ukrainian forces who will go on to operate these tanks.{{cite news|last=Aiello|first=Rachel|title=Canada sending 4 tanks to Ukraine and deploying soldiers to train, defence minister says|url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/canada-sending-4-tanks-to-ukraine-and-deploying-soldiers-to-train-defence-minister-says-1.6247335|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230126174702/https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/canada-sending-4-tanks-to-ukraine-and-deploying-soldiers-to-train-defence-minister-says-1.6247335|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 January 2023|access-date=2023-01-26|work=CTV News|date=2023-01-26}} The first Canadian Leopard 2 tanks had arrived in Poland on 5 February, to allow Ukrainian troops to begin training.{{cite news|title=Kyiv says new attacks are being planned by Moscow|url=https://www.euronews.com/2023/02/05/canadian-leopard-2-tanks-en-route-to-ukraine-as-troops-prepare-for-suspected-moscow-attack|access-date=2023-02-15|work=euronews|date=2023-02-05|language=en}} On 24 February, the Canadian [[Prime Minister of Canada|Prime Minister]], [[Justin Trudeau]], announced that Canada would be sending a further four Leopard 2A4 tanks to Ukraine along with one armoured recovery vehicle (ARV) and 5,000 rounds of ammunition.{{cite news|title=Canada sending four more battle tanks, ammunition to Ukraine|url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/canada-sending-four-more-battle-tanks-to-ukraine-1.6288251|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230224200017/https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/canada-sending-four-more-battle-tanks-to-ukraine-1.6288251|url-status=dead|archive-date=24 February 2023|access-date=2023-02-24|work=CTV News|date=2023-02-24}} =====Czech Republic===== On 20 January 2023, the Czech Defense Ministry issued a statement that the media reports indicating the Czech Republic and Slovakia were willing to give up their Leopard 2 tanks for Ukraine were false, and that rumors that the Czech Republic would receive American Abrams tanks in exchange for Leopards were also false.{{cite web|title=The agreement on Leopard tanks applies to the Czech Republic|url=https://mocr.army.cz/informacni-servis/zpravodajstvi/dohoda-o-tancich-leopard-pro-cr-plati-241773/|access-date=2023-02-26|website=Ministry of Defense of Czech Republic|date=2023-01-20|language=cs}} As of December 2022, both countries had only received one Leopard 2A4 each from Rheinmetall as part of Germany's ''Ringtausch'' program in exchange for them delivering older Soviet equipment to Ukraine, while the remaining Leopard 2A4s are still being refurbished (expected to be delivered throughout 2023).{{cite web|title=Armáda převzala první z německých Leopardů. Zda koupí další, ukáže studie|trans-title=The army took delivery of the first of the German Leopards. The study will show whether they will buy more|website=iDNES.cz|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/nato/leopard-armada-praslavice-cernochova-ukrajina-tank.A221220_202604_zpr_nato_inc|date=2022-12-21|language=cs}} =====Denmark===== While it was reported in the international press that Denmark had signalled that it could contribute a number of tanks, there was no official indication from the Danish Government that any Danish Leopard 2s would be sent to Ukraine. Of the Danish inventory of 44 tanks, 14 were deployed to Estonia as part of [[NATO Enhanced Forward Presence|NATO EFP]], with a further number receiving upgrades at the German manufacturers.{{cite news|last1=Jungersen|first1=Rasmus|last2=Tørnqvist|first2=Tim|title='Vi sender ikke alt afsted': Danske Leopard-kampvogne bliver endnu ikke sendt til Ukraine|url=https://www.dr.dk/nyheder/politik/vi-sender-ikke-alt-afsted-danske-leopard-kampvogne-bliver-endnu-ikke-sendt-til|trans-title='We are not sending everything': Danish Leopard tanks are not yet being sent to Ukraine|access-date=2023-01-28|work=DR|publisher=Danish Broadcasting Corporation|language=da|date=2023-01-19}} Some Danish opposition politicians voiced support for a transfer of Danish tanks.{{cite news|last=Bugge|first=Mathilde|title=Partier åbner for at sende Danmarks bedste kampvogne til Ukraine|url=https://www.dr.dk/nyheder/politik/partier-aabner-sende-danmarks-bedste-kampvogne-til-ukraine|trans-title=Parties open to send Denmark's best tanks to Ukraine|access-date=2023-01-28|work=DR|publisher=Danish Broadcasting Corporation|date=2023-01-25|language=da}} Unlike those considered by other countries, the Danish Leopards are of the new 2A7 standard, which would represent some logistic and mechanical challenges compared to the other variants.{{cite news|title=Hvis alle sender kampvogne, bliver det et gedemarked, siger militæranalytiker|trans-title=If everyone sends tanks, it will be a goat market, military analyst says|url=https://nyheder.tv2.dk/udland/2023-01-31-hvis-alle-sender-kampvogne-bliver-det-et-gedemarked-siger-militaeranalytiker|date=2023-01-31|website=TV2|access-date=2023-02-03|language=da}} Denmark instead announced on 7 February that it was jointly purchasing 100-178 Leopard 1A5 tanks with Germany and the Netherlands.{{cite news|title=Ukraine to Get as Many as 178 Leopard 1 Tanks From EU Allies|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-02-07/germany-denmark-netherlands-to-send-kyiv-178-leopard-1-tanks|access-date=2023-02-26|work=Bloomberg|date=2023-02-07}} Denmark also announced on 20 April 2023 that they would jointly finance with the Netherlands the purchase and refurbishing of 14 Leopard 2A4 for Ukraine from private industry stocks.{{cite web|date=2023-04-20|title=Danmark og Nederlandene indgår samarbejde om donation af Leopard 2-kampvogne til Ukraine|url=https://www.fmn.dk/da/nyheder/2023/danmark-og-nederlandene-indgar-samarbejde-om-donation-af-leopard-2-kampvogne-til-ukraine/|website=Danish Ministry of Defense|language=da}} =====Finland===== Finland had suggested before the German decision on reexport, that it could supply Ukraine with a limited number of Leopard 2 tanks. [[President of Finland|The Finnish President]], [[Sauli Niinistö]], warned that "the number of tanks [to be sent to Ukraine] cannot be large, since Finland borders on Russia and is not part of NATO [yet]."{{cite news|last=Sorgi|first=Gregorio|title=Finland could deliver Leopard tanks to Ukraine, its president says|url=https://www.politico.eu/article/finland-leopard-2-tanks-ukraine-sauli-niinisto-nato-defense/|access-date=2023-01-25|work=Politico|date=2023-01-12}} On 23 February Finland announced it will give three of its six Leopard 2R breaching tanks to Ukraine.{{cite web|date=2023-02-23|title=Suomi luovuttaa Ukrainalle kolme Leopard 2 -raivausvaunua: "Etulinjan vehkeitä – varma taistelukentän työjuhta"|url=https://www.mtvuutiset.fi/artikkeli/suomi-luovuttaa-ukrainalle-kolme-leopard-2-raivausvaunua/8639832|access-date=2023-02-24|website=mtvuutiset.fi|language=fi}} The donation of the remaining three was announced a month later.{{cite web|title=Finland donates defence materiel assistance to Ukraine including more of mine-clearing Leopard 2 tanks|url=https://www.defmin.fi/en/topical/press_releases_and_news/press_release_archive/2023/finland_donates_defence_materiel_assistance_to_ukraine_including_more_of_mine-clearing_leopard_2_tanks.13477.news|date=2023-03-23|access-date=2024-04-20|website=Ministry of Defence|language=en}} =====Greece===== On 25 January 2023 it was reported that Greece was one of the countries that had indicated it would supply Leopard 2 tanks to Ukraine.{{cite web|date=2023-01-25|title=Explained: Ukraine Will Get Leopard Tanks, What Happens Next?|url=https://www.kyivpost.com/post/11499|access-date=2023-02-26|website=Kyiv Post|language=en}} On 29 January 2023 it was erroneously reported that approximately 14 Leopard 2 tanks would be provided, though it was unclear if it would be the 2A4 or 2A6 HEL variant.{{cite web|date=2023-01-29|title=Greece to send Leopard-2 tanks to Ukraine|url=https://greekcitytimes.com/2023/01/29/greece-to-send-leopard-2-tanks-to-ukraine/|access-date=2023-02-26|website=Greek City Times|language=en}} However, on 31 January, Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis clarified that Greece would not supply any Leopard tanks to Ukraine, arguing "they are absolutely necessary for our defense posture."{{cite web|date=2023-01-31|last1=Take|first1=Sayumi|last2=Sharp|first2=Andrew|title=Greek PM slams Turkey for 'sitting on the fence' over Ukraine war|url=https://asia.nikkei.com/Editor-s-Picks/Interview/Greek-PM-slams-Turkey-for-sitting-on-the-fence-over-Ukraine-war|access-date=2023-02-26|website=Nikkei Asia}} [[2023 Pentagon document leaks|Leaked Pentagon documents]] revealed that Greece was preparing to donate five of its Leopard 2 tanks to Ukraine, though Greek defense minister Nikolaos Panayiotopoulos reiterated later in April his government's opposition to tank deliveries to Ukraine, making confirmation of the delivery uncertain.{{cite web|date=2023-04-25|title=Ukrainian Tankers Would Love To Get Their Hands On Ex-Greek Leopard 2A6HELs. Politics Might Disappoint Them|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/davidaxe/2023/04/25/ukrainian-tankers-would-love-to-get-their-hands-on-ex-greek-leopard-2a6hels-politics-might-disappoint-them/?sh=4d0d48bd2f18|first=David|last=Axe|website=Forbes}} =====Netherlands===== The Netherlands was considering Ukrainian requests for Leopard 2 tanks, with [[Prime Minister of the Netherlands|Prime Minister]] [[Mark Rutte]] suggesting that the [[Dutch government]] could purchase tanks from other countries and donate them.{{cite news|title=Netherlands considering providing Ukraine with Leopard 2 tanks|url=https://nltimes.nl/2023/01/25/netherlands-considering-providing-ukraine-leopard-2-tanks|access-date=2023-01-25|work=NL Times|date=2023-01-25}} There were also some discussions about Netherlands purchasing the 18 Leopard 2A6 tanks they lease from Germany. No refusal was made from Germany to sell them as no formal request to buy them was made; both countries agreed that they were critical to the operations of the joint German-Dutch military unit. However, the Netherlands agreed to supply ammunition for Leopard tanks and announced it had not abandoned its intention to contribute to the tank initiative, while also noting it was helping to purchase Leopard 1A5 tanks with Denmark and Germany.{{cite news|title=Netherlands says still supports tank deliveries for Ukraine|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/netherlands-says-still-supports-tank-deliveries-ukraine-2023-02-15/|date=2023-02-15|website=Reuters|access-date=2023-02-26}} The Netherlands later announced it was jointly financing with Denmark the purchase and refurbishing of 14 Leopard 2A4 for Ukraine from private industry stocks, with delivery expected in early 2024.{{cite web|date=2023-04-20|title=More Leopards for Ukraine: Denmark, Netherlands to send 14 tanks|url=https://www.politico.eu/article/denmark-netherlands-to-donate-14-leopard-2-tanks-to-ukraine/|website=Politico}} =====Norway===== On 25 January 2023, Norway pledged to donate spare Leopards to Ukraine with reports speculating that between four and eight of its 36 Leopard 2A4 tanks would be sent.{{cite news|last=Axe|first=David|title=Leopard 2 Tanks From All Over Europe Are Heading To Ukraine As German Resistance Collapses|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/davidaxe/2023/01/24/leopard-2-tanks-from-all-over-europe-are-heading-to-ukraine-as-german-resistance-collapses/|access-date=2023-01-25|work=Forbes|date=2023-01-24}}{{cite news|title=Norway considering sending Leopard 2 tanks to Ukraine: Media|url=https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2023/01/25/Norway-considering-sending-Leopard-2-tanks-to-Ukraine-Media-|access-date=2023-01-25|work=Al Arabiya News|date=2023-01-25}}{{cite news|last1=Gjerstad|first1=Tore|last2=Melgård|first2=Marie|title=Opplysninger til DN: Norge kan gi Ukraina opptil åtte stridsvogner|trans-title=Information to DN: Norway can give Ukraine up to eight tanks|url=https://www.dn.no/politikk/stridsvogner/krigen-i-ukraina/opplysninger-til-dn-norge-kan-gi-ukraina-opptil-atte-stridsvogner/2-1-1392690|access-date=2023-01-25|work=[[Dagens Næringsliv|DN]]|date=2023-01-24|language=no}} Norwegian defence minister [[Bjørn Arild Gram]] said in an interview with Norwegian public television [[NRK]]: "Norway and the government support the donation of battle tanks to Ukraine. Norway will take part," but did not specify how many would be sent.{{cite news|last1=Gambino|first1=Lauren|last2=Smith|first2=David|title=US joins Germany in sending tanks to Ukraine as Biden hails 'united' effort|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2023/jan/25/us-m1-abrams-biden-tanks-ukraine-russia-war|access-date=2023-01-26|work=The Guardian|date=2023-01-25}} On 14 February 2023, Gram announced that 8 Norwegian Leopard 2 tanks and 4 Leopard 1 derived "special purpose vehicles" would be handed over to Ukraine. The special purpose vehicles turned out to be a mix of 3 NM189 AEVs and 1 NM217 ARV.{{cite news|title=Norway details Leopard 2 donation to Ukraine|url=https://www.shephardmedia.com/news/landwarfareintl/norway-donating-tank-package-to-ukraine/|access-date=2023-02-15|work=Shephard}}{{cite web|title=Norway with comprehensive tanks-package to Ukraine|date=2023-02-14|url=https://www.regjeringen.no/en/aktuelt/brusselnyhet/id2963053/|website=Norwegian Government|access-date=2023-03-02|quote=The decision to donate Leopard 2-tanks and special purpose tanks has been made after close dialogue with both the Chief of Defence and other European countries.}} In February 2023, Norway ordered 54 Leopard 2A7 tanks (later changed to 2A8 variant) to be delivered from 2026, with a further option for 18 vehicles if necessary. =====Portugal===== When the German government changed its position on the reexport of Leopard 2 tanks, it was reported that the Portuguese government was preparing to send four of their Leopard 2A6 tanks to Ukraine.{{cite news|last=Gonçalves|first=Francisco J.|title=Portugal prepara envio de quatro tanques para a Ucrânia|trans-title=Portugal prepares to send four tanks to Ukraine|url=https://www.cmjornal.pt/mundo/detalhe/portugal-prepara-envio-de-quatro-tanques-para-a-ucrania|access-date=2023-01-25|work=Correio da Manhã|date=2023-01-25|language=pt}} On 4 February, [[Prime Minister of Portugal|Prime Minister]] [[António Costa]] confirmed that Portugal would send Leopards to Ukraine, but did not confirm the number of vehicles set to be delivered. It is understood that Portugal is working with Germany to obtain the necessary parts to repair inoperable tanks in its inventory of 37 Leopard 2 tanks, but it has been widely reported by local media that most are inoperable. Costa expressed hopes that Portuguese tanks would be delivered by March 2023.{{cite news|title=Portugal to send Leopard tanks to Ukraine, PM says|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/portugal-send-leopard-tanks-ukraine-pm-says-2023-02-04/|access-date=2023-02-04|work=Reuters|date=2023-02-04}} On 14 February, it was reported that Portugal had earmarked three Leopard 2A6 tanks for donation to Ukraine. All three were confirmed donated on 27 March together with the 18 German Leopard 2A6.{{cite web|date=2023-04-27|title=Answering The Call: Heavy Weaponry Supplied To Ukraine|url=https://www.oryxspioenkop.com/2022/04/answering-call-heavy-weaponry-supplied.html|website=Oryx}} =====Slovakia===== On 25 January 2023, Slovakia announced it was not considering the transfer of any of its Leopard 2A4 tanks to Ukraine, but were willing to provide T-72 tanks if other allies replaced them with other tanks. The reason cited for this was that Slovakia had only received 1 of the 15 Leopard tanks it was promised as part of Germany's ''Ringtaush'' program, which it was getting in exchange for supplying Ukraine with 30 Soviet-era infantry fighting vehicles.{{cite news|title=Slovakia does not plan to supply Ukraine with Leopard 2, but ready to provide T-72 instead|url=https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2023/01/25/7386530/|access-date=2023-02-15|work=Ukrainska Pravda|date=2023-01-25}} =====Spain===== On 4 June 2022 it was reported that Spain was considering providing 40 of its 53 retired Leopard 2A4 tanks stored in Zaragoza.{{cite news|title=España, dispuesta a entregar a Ucrania misiles antiaéreos y carros de combate Leopard|trans-title=Spain, ready to deliver anti-aircraft missiles and Leopard tanks to Ukraine|url=https://elpais.com/espana/2022-06-05/espana-dispuesta-a-entregar-a-ucrania-misiles-antiaereos-y-carros-de-combate-leopard.html|access-date=2023-03-24|work=El Pais|last=González|first=Miguel|date=2022-06-05|language=es}} On 8 June German Chancellor Olaf Scholz denied receiving any formal request from Spain for an export permit for Leopard 2 tanks to Ukraine.{{cite news|title=Germany to boost military mission in Lithuania|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/germanys-scholz-pledges-boost-military-mission-lithuania-2022-06-07/2022-08-02/|access-date=2023-03-24|work=Reuters|date=2022-06-08}} However it was Ukraine|url=https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20220610-spain-mulls-whether-to-send-high-tech-tanks-to-ukraine|access-date=2023-03-24|work=France24|date=2022-06-10|language=en}} On 12 June, anonymous government sources told Der Spiegel that the Scholz government blocked any transfer of Leopard tanks to Ukraine, arguing this "would constitute a departure" from an informal NATO decision not to Ukraine|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/spain-says-its-mothballed-german-made-tanks-no-fit-state-send-ukraine-2022-08-02/|access-date=2023-03-24|work=Reuters|date=2022-08-02}} The Spanish news|last1=González|first1=Miguel|title=España se suma al plan europeo para entregar tanques Leopard a Ucrania|trans-title=Spain joins the European plan to deliver Leopard tanks to news|url=https://www.zeit.de/politik/ausland/2023-02/ukraine-ueberblick-norwegen-panzer-nato-ramstein-bachmut|title=Norwegen will Panzer liefern, Ramstein-Treffen ohne neue Zusagen|trans-title=Norway web|url=https://www.epe.es/es/internacional/20230205/espana-reforzara-letalidad-tanques-leopard-guerra-ucrania-82519615|title=España reforzará la letalidad de sus tanques Leopard antes de enviarlos a ===Beyond Europe=== In 2005, [[Turkish Armed Forces|Turkey]] ordered 298 Leopard 2 tanks from German army stocks.{{cite news|title=Germany to Sell 298 Leopard 2 Tanks to Turkey|url=http://www.defenseindustrydaily.com/germany-to-sell-298-leopard-2-tanks-to-turkey-01473/|access-date=2016-01-11|publisher=defenseindustrydaily.com|date=2005-11-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160122093943/http://www.defenseindustrydaily.com/germany-to-sell-298-leopard-2-tanks-to-turkey-01473/|archive-date=2016-01-22|url-status=live}} Turkey wanted to buy 1,000 Leopard 2 tanks in 1999, but the German government rejected the deal. ===KFOR=== [[File:Slt Elefant.jpg|thumb|A German Leopard 2A4 being unloaded from a [[SLT 50 Elefant]] tank transporter in Kosovo, July 2002]] Starting on 12 June 1999, 28 Leopard 2A5 tanks were deployed to Kosovo by the German Army as part of the [[Kosovo Force]] (KFOR). The vehicles of Panzerbataillon 33 and 214 were sent from [[North Macedonia]] to [[Prizren]]. They were used for patrols, protecting checkpoints and bases as well as part of the [[show of force]]. On 13 June 1999, two members of the [[Serbia]]n paramilitary [[Prizren incident (1999)|started firing]] from inside a [[Fiat 125p]] car at one of the checkpoints in Prizren and both were killed by return fire. A Leopard 2A5 was located at the checkpoint, but it could not participate in the fighting as it was only partially crewed.{{cite web|url=http://www.spiegel.de/politik/ausland/0,1518,27113,00.html|title=Kosovo: Schießerei am deutschen Kontrollpunkt|trans-title=Kosovo: shooting at German checkpoint|website=Spiegel Online|date=1999-06-14|language=de|access-date=2016-01-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130510014656/http://www.spiegel.de/politik/ausland/kosovo-schiesserei-am-deutschen-kontrollpunkt-a-27113.html|archive-date=2013-05-10|url-status=live}} On 26 June 1999, a Leopard 2A5 fired four warning shots above the town of [[Orahovac, Kosovo|Orahovac]].{{cite book|first=Frank|last=Lobitz|title=Kampfpanzer Leopard 2. Entwicklung und Einsatz in der Bundeswehr|trans-title=Leopard main battle tank 2. Development and German Army Service|publisher=Tankograd Publishing – Verlag Jochen Vollert|year=2009|page=229 et seq|language=de|isbn=978-3-936519-08-2}} From late 2000 to early 2001, the tanks were replaced by the Leopard 2A4 model. Leopard 2A4s were deployed to North Macedonia in 2001 as part of the NATO intervention. The tanks served to protect Bundeswehr logistic sites in North Macedonia. Until their return in 2004, the Leopard 2 tanks were stationed at the Austrian-Swiss camp "Casablanca". ===IFOR/SFOR=== The Dutch contingent in [[Bosnia-Herzegovina]] operated Leopard 2 tanks.Jerchel, p. 37. Dutch Leopard 2A4s and Leopard 2A5s were stationed at the NLD bases at [[Bugojno]], [[Novi Travnik]], [[Sisava]], [[Kneževo, Bosnia and Herzegovina|Knezevo]], [[Maslovare]] and [[Šujica, Tomislavgrad|Suica]].{{citation needed|date=August 2013}} ===ISAF/OEF=== In October 2003, Canada was planning to replace its [[Leopard C2]]s with wheeled [[Stryker Mobile Gun System]]s. However, operational experience in [[Afghanistan]] and in particular during [[Operation Medusa]], convinced the [[Canadian military]] of the usefulness of maintaining a tank fleet.{{cite news|title=Tanks for the Lesson: Leopards, too, for Canada|url=http://www.defenseindustrydaily.com/tanks-for-the-lesson-leopards-too-for-canada-03208/#choices|work=Defense Industry Daily|date=December 2006|access-date=2009-01-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130113205328/http://www.defenseindustrydaily.com/tanks-for-the-lesson-leopards-too-for-canada-03208/%23choices/|archive-date=2013-01-13|url-status=live}} Leopard C2s were deployed to [[Kandahar]] in December 2006,{{cite news|first=Stephen|last=Priestley|title=In to Action – Canadian Leopard C2 tanks and the TLAV M113A3s in Combat|url=http://www.casr.ca/ft-leopard-tank.htm|publisher=[[Canadian American Strategic Review]]|date=2008-10-08|access-date=2009-01-08|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100109063605/http://casr.ca/ft-leopard-tank.htm|archive-date=2010-01-09}} but they were by then almost 30 years old, and were nearing the end of their operational life. The Canadian government decided to borrow 20 Leopard 2A6s and three [[armoured recovery vehicle]]s from Germany for rapid deployment to Afghanistan. In late August 2007, the first Leopard 2s were airlifted into Afghanistan to equip [[Lord Strathcona's Horse (Royal Canadians)]].{{cite news|first=Brian|last=Corbett|title=Canada's new main battle tank—Leopard 2|url=http://www.forces.gc.ca/site/community/mapleleaf/vol_10/vol10_27/1027_07.pdf|publisher=The Maple Leaf|date=2007-09-19|access-date=2009-01-08|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090225074757/http://www.forces.gc.ca/site/community/mapleleaf/vol_10/vol10_27/1027_07.pdf|archive-date=2009-02-25}} In an assault on 2 November 2007, a Leopard 2A6M hit an [[improvised explosive device]] (IED) and survived without casualties: "My crew stumbled upon an IED (improvised explosive device) and made history as the first (crew) to test the (Leopard 2A6) M-packet. It worked as it should", wrote a Canadian officer in an email to German defence officials.{{cite news|url=http://www.dailyheraldtribune.com/ArticleDisplay.aspx?archive=true&e=2378441|title=Germany gets a thank-you from Canadian IED survivor|publisher=Grand Prairie Daily Herald-Tribune|date=2007-12-06|access-date=2010-10-27|url-status=dead}}{{New archival link needed|date=April 2026}} Canadian Chief of the Defence Staff General [[Rick Hillier]] denied reports that a Leopard 2 tank that was struck by an IED was a write-off, insisting that the tank has been repaired and is once again in use. "The Taliban have been engaged with some of the new Leopard 2 tanks in several ambushes" and that as a result the [[Taliban]] "learned some very harsh lessons" and lost the battle in question "very quickly and very violently."{{cite news|first=Alan|last=Freeman|title=Tank hit by IED back in service: Hillier|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/world/tank-hit-by-ied-back-in-service-hillier/article20406656/|publisher=[[The Globe and Mail]]|date=2007-12-08|access-date=2008-07-31|location=Toronto}} In October 2007, Denmark deployed Leopard 2A5 DKs in support of operations in southern Afghanistan. The Danish tank unit, drawn from the first battalion of the ''[[Jydske Dragonregiment]]'' (Jutland Dragoons Regiment),{{cite web|url=http://www.casr.ca/ft-leopard-2a5-denmark.htm|title=The Danish Army is Prepared to Deploy Tanks to Helmand Province|access-date=2009-01-09|last=Priestley|first=Stephen|date=May 2007|publisher=[[Canadian American Strategic Review]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081216170241/http://www.casr.ca/ft-leopard-2a5-denmark.htm|archive-date=2008-12-16}} was equipped with three tanks and one [[M113 armored personnel carrier|M113 armoured personnel carrier]], with an armoured recovery vehicle and another tank kept in reserve.{{cite web|url=http://www.nato.int/multi/2007/071121b-afghan-stories/video/071121b-01.wmv|title=Danish tanks arrive in Afghanistan|access-date=2008-12-15|publisher=[[NATO]]|date=2008-11-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218111409/http://www.nato.int/multi/2007/071121b-afghan-stories/video/071121b-01.wmv|archive-date=2008-12-18|url-status=live}} The Danish version of the Leopard 2A5 is fitted with Swedish-made Barracuda camouflage mats that limit the absorption of solar heat, thus reducing infrared signature and interior temperature. It also has a conventional driver's seat bolted on the floor of the tank, whereas in the Canadian 2A6M (as part of the mine-protection package) the driver's seat has been replaced by a "dynamic safety seat",{{cite web|url=http://www.europaeische-sicherheit.de/Ausgaben/2008/2008_01/Umschau/2008,01,umschau.html|title=LEOPARD 2 bewährt sich gegen IEDs|access-date=2009-01-07|date=January 2008|publisher=Europäische Sicherheit|language=de|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090111052006/http://www.europaeische-sicherheit.de/Ausgaben/2008/2008_01/Umschau/2008,01,umschau.html|archive-date=2009-01-11}} which is a parachute-harness like arrangement that the driver wears around his hip. This way, the driver does not have any contact with the hull except on the pedals and is out of the shockwave area of exploding land mines or IEDs. In January 2008, Danish tanks halted a flanking manoeuvre by Taliban forces near the [[Helmand River]] by providing gunfire in support of Danish and British infantry from elevated positions.{{cite web|url=http://www.casr.ca/ft-leopard-2a5-denmark-2.htm|title=Danish Leopard tanks in supporting action in Helmand Province: Can Open Government be measured by a Military Press Release?|access-date=2008-07-31|last=Stephen|first=Priestley|date=January 2008|publisher=[[Canadian American Strategic Review]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080930180306/http://www.casr.ca/ft-leopard-2a5-denmark-2.htm|archive-date=2008-09-30}} On 26 February 2008, a Danish Leopard 2 was hit by an explosive device, damaging one track. No one was injured and the tank returned to camp on its own for repairs.{{cite news|first=Eckart|last=Lohse|title=Leopardenjagd am Hindukusch|url=https://www.faz.net/s/RubDDBDABB9457A437BAA85A49C26FB23A0/Doc~E74D84BBBF12B478BBD4C7901BB39BF59~ATpl~Ecommon~Scontent.html|publisher=[[Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung]]|date=2008-03-16|access-date=2008-07-31|page=6|language=de|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080704212849/https://www.faz.net/s/RubDDBDABB9457A437BAA85A49C26FB23A0/Doc~E74D84BBBF12B478BBD4C7901BB39BF59~ATpl~Ecommon~Scontent.html|archive-date=2008-07-04|url-status=dead}} The first fatality suffered by a crew operating a Leopard 2 happened on 25 July 2008. A Danish Leopard 2A5 hit an IED in [[Helmand Province]]. The vehicle was able to continue {{cvt|200|m|ft}} before it halted.{{cite web|url=http://forsvaret.dk/HOK/Nyt%20og%20Presse/ISAF/Pages/Statusoverfredagensbegivenheder.aspx|title=Status over fredagens begivenheder – Afghanistan: Alle danske soldater er nu tilbage i deres respektive lejre i Helmand provinsen|access-date=2008-07-31|publisher=[[Royal Danish Army]]|date=2008-07-25|language=da|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091017063251/http://forsvaret.dk/HOK/Nyt%20og%20Presse/ISAF/Pages/Statusoverfredagensbegivenheder.aspx|archive-date=2009-10-17}} Three members of the four-man crew were able to escape even though wounded, but the driver was stuck inside. Onsite treatment by Danish medics could not save him. The vehicle was towed to [[Forward Operating Base]] (FOB) Attal and then later to FOB Armadillo for investigation and possible redeployment. During the same contact with Taliban forces, a second tank was caught in an explosion but none of the crew were wounded. Beginning on 7 December 2008, Leopard 2 tanks took part in [[Operation Red Dagger]], firing 31 rounds in support of Coalition troops as they recaptured [[Nad Ali District]]. A press release from the [[Ministry of Defence (United Kingdom)|British Ministry of Defence]] praised the tank's fire accuracy and mobility, claiming the Leopard 2 was a decisive factor in the coalition's success.{{cite web|url=http://www.mod.uk/DefenceInternet/DefenceNews/MilitaryOperations/InPicturesOpRedDaggerStrikesInHelmand.htm|title=In Pictures: Op Red Dagger strikes in Helmand (mod.uk)|access-date=2009-01-10|archive-date=2009-01-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090107225202/http://www.mod.uk/DefenceInternet/DefenceNews/MilitaryOperations/InPicturesOpRedDaggerStrikesInHelmand.htm|url-status=dead}} ===Turkish intervention in Syria=== Turkey operates 354 Leopard 2A4 tanks. Initially using other tank types including upgraded [[M60 tank|M60s]], in December 2016 Turkey deployed a number of Leopard 2A4s to the [[Syrian Civil War]] against [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant]] (ISIS) as part of [[Operation Euphrates Shield]].{{citation needed|date=December 2020}} Initially, three of the Turkish Leopard 2A4s operating in Syria were destroyed or damaged by ISIS using anti-tank missile systems (possibly [[9K111 Fagot|Fagot]] or [[9M113 Konkurs|Konkurs]] anti-tank guided missiles obtained from [[Syrian Army|Syrian]] or [[Iraqi Army]] captured stocks).{{citation needed|date=December 2020}} In mid-December 2016, two 2A4 tanks were captured by ISIS [[Battle of al-Bab|near al-Bab city]] in Syria during Euphrates Shield operations. [[Amaq News Agency]] posted video of vehicles claimed to be captured Leopard 2A4s.{{cite news|url=http://www.middleeasteye.net/news/claims-capture-two-tanks-after-killing-70-turkish-troops-syria-845385252|title=Islamic State: We captured Turkish tanks in Syria battle|agency=Middle East Eye|date=2016-12-22|access-date=2017-01-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161226221245/http://www.middleeasteye.net/news/claims-capture-two-tanks-after-killing-70-turkish-troops-syria-845385252|archive-date=2016-12-26|url-status=live}} By late December 2016, ISIS had captured or incapacitated 10 Leopard 2A4s. These were damaged by anti-tank weapons, IEDs, or other unknown causes.{{cite web|title=Турецкие потери в технике в Сирии|work=BMPD|date=2016-12-25|language=ru|url=http://bmpd.livejournal.com/2343546.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161227172433/http://bmpd.livejournal.com/2343546.html|archive-date=2016-12-27|url-status=live}}{{cite web|url=http://www.focus.de/politik/videos/schwachstelle-entdeckt-verluste-in-syrien-ein-deutscher-panzer-mythos-wird-jetzt-zerstoert_id_6487678.html|title=Er galt als unzerstörbar: In Syrien wird ein Panzer-Mythos zerstört|work=Focus|language=de|date=2017-01-12|access-date=2017-01-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170113110948/http://www.focus.de/politik/videos/schwachstelle-entdeckt-verluste-in-syrien-ein-deutscher-panzer-mythos-wird-jetzt-zerstoert_id_6487678.html|archive-date=2017-01-13|url-status=live}} Additional ISIS propaganda images and video depicting several completely destroyed Leopards, some with their [[Jack-in-the-box effect|turrets blown off]], were published in January 2017.{{cite web|author=Leith Fadel|url=https://www.almasdarnews.com/article/turkish-army-suffers-heavy-casualties-failed-east-aleppo-offensive/|title=Turkish Army suffers heavy casualties in failed east Aleppo offensive|work=Al-Masdar News|date=2017-01-20|access-date=2017-01-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170120205256/https://www.almasdarnews.com/article/turkish-army-suffers-heavy-casualties-failed-east-aleppo-offensive/|archive-date=2017-01-20|url-status=dead}} The 'turret blown off' effect was potentially caused by a quirk of the Leopard's design, with only 15 rounds being stored in blow-out panel compartments (27 other rounds stored in the forward section of the hull, to the left of the driver's station, they were cause to catastrophic secondary explosions).{{cite web|url=https://tank-afv.com/coldwar/West_Germany/leopard-2.php|title=West German cold war KMW Leopard 2 MBT (1978)|first=David|last=Bocquelet|website=tank-afv.com|access-date=2023-12-21}} Tanks which suffered the worst damage may have been destroyed by airstrikes in order to prevent capture but sources generally state that the damage was caused solely with anti-tank missiles or [[SVBIED|car bombs driven by suicide bombers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bellingcat.com/news/mena/2017/02/12/battle-al-bab-verifying-turkish-military-vehicle-losses/|title=The Battle for Al-Bab: Verifying Euphrates Shield Vehicle Losses – These tanks were designed during the Cold War to fight against Soviet tanks in Europe, not counterinsurgencies against guerrillas, where the primary risk is improvised explosive devices and anti-tank missiles. These tanks were retired from German usage when sold to Turkey.{{cite web|url=https://nationalinterest.org/blog/buzz/turkeys-leopard-2-tanks-are-getting-crushed-syria-95396?amp|title=Turkey's Leopard 2 Tanks Are Getting Crushed in Syria|date=2019-11-09|access-date=2023-01-21}}{{cite news|url=https://de.reuters.com/article/deutschland-t-rkei-panzer-idDEKBN1FI1R2?il=0|title=Türkei bestätigt der Bundesregierung Einsatz von Leopard-Panzern|work=DE|access-date=2018-01-29|language=de-DE|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180130091236/https://de.reuters.com/article/deutschland-t-rkei-panzer-idDEKBN1FI1R2?il=0|archive-date=2018-01-30|url-status=dead}} There is a belief that the Turkish purchase of Leopard 2A4s from Germany was subject to the condition that they were not to be used against Kurdish separatists. Prior to 2016, the Leopard 2A4s were kept in northern Turkey. Once the German government discovered that the Leopard tanks were being used against Kurdish forces, planned upgrades to make them "less vulnerable to explosives" were halted. The Russian column was led by two "[[turtle tank]]s" fitted with bulky anti-drone armour.{{Cite web |last=Axe |first=David |title=A Ukrainian Leopard 2 Tank Met A Russian Armored Column Head-On—And Wrecked It |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/davidaxe/2024/11/13/a-ukrainian-leopard-2-tank-met-a-russian-armored-column-head-on-and-wrecked-it/ |access-date=2024-11-16 |website=Forbes |language=en}}{{better source needed|date=November 2024}} As of 1 July 2025, according to the analysis of photos, videos and other visual evidence performed and reported in the [[Oryx (website)|Oryx blog]], at least 24 Ukrainian Leopard 2s of various models were destroyed (13 Leopard 2A4/2A4V, 7 Leopard 2A6, 1 Strv 122, 2 Bergepanzer-3, 1 Leopard 2R); while another 31 were confirmed damaged to various degrees or abandoned by their crews or captured by Russians: 14 Leopard 2A4/2A4V (6 damaged, 6 abandoned, 2 captured), 6 Leopard 2A6 (4 damaged, 1 abandoned, 1 captured), 8 Strv 122 (2 damaged, 6 abandoned) and 3 Leopard 2R (2 damaged, 1 abandoned).{{cite web |url=https://www.oryxspioenkop.com/2022/02/attack-on-europe-documenting-ukrainian.html |website=oryxspioenkop.com |title=Documenting Ukrainian Equipment Losses During The Russian Invasion Of Ukraine |access-date=1 July 2025 }} ==Variants== {{overly detailed|section|date=June 2024}} ===Leopard 2=== [[File:Zwei Leopard 2A5 beim durchqueren eines Gewässer.ogv|thumb|Two [[German Army]] Leopard 2A5s demonstrate their [[Deep wading|deep-wading]] capabilities.]] The baseline Leopard 2, sometimes informally called the "A0" to differentiate it from later versions, was the first series manufactured version. The vehicles were manufactured from October 1979 until March 1982, altogether 380 vehicles. 209 were built by Krauss Maffei and 171 by MaK. The basic equipment consisted of electrical-hydraulic stabiliser WNA-H22, a fire control computer, a laser rangefinder, a wind sensor, a general-purpose telescope EMES 15, a panorama periscope PERI R17, the gunner's primary sight FERO Z18, on the turret roof as well as a computer-controlled tank testing set RPP 1–8. 200 of the vehicles had a low-light enhancer (PZB 200) instead of thermal imaging. Two chassis served as driver training vehicles.{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} ===Leopard 2A1=== Minor modifications and the installation of the gunner's thermal sight{{cite book|last=Gelbart|first=Marsh|title=Tanks: main battle and light tanks|year=1996|publisher=Brassey's UK|pages=109–10|isbn=978-1-85753-168-8|oclc=36171829}} were worked into the second batch of 450 vehicles Leopard 2, designated the A1. Krauss-Maffei built 248 (Chassis Nr. 10211 to 10458) and MaK built 202 (Chassis Nr. 20173 to 20347). Deliveries of the ''2A1'' models started in March 1982 and ended in November 1983. The two most notable changes were the modification of the ammunition racks to be identical to those in the M1A1 Abrams, and redesigned fuel filters that reduce refuelling time.{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} A third batch of 300 Leopard 2, 165 by Krauss-Maffei (Chassis Nr. 10459 to 10623) and 135 by MaK (Chassis Nr. 20375 to 20509.), was built between November 1983 and November 1984. This batch included more minor changes that were later retrofitted to the earlier 2A1s.{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} ===Leopard 2A2=== This designation was given to upgraded vehicles of the first batch of Leopard 2s, brought up to the standard of the second and third batches. This modernisation gradually replaced the original PZB 200 sights in the first batch with thermal sights for the EMES 15 as they became available. The upgrade included the fitting of filler openings and caps to the forward hull fuel tanks to allow separate refuelling. There was an addition of a deflector plate for the periscope and a large cover plate to protect the existing NBC protection system. The tank was given new five metre towing cables with a different position. The programme began in 1984 and ended in 1987. The third, fourth and fifth batches, which were produced during this period, had the same features. The modernised first batch can be recognised by the circular plate covering the hole where the crosswind sensor for the fire control system was removed.{{cite book|last1=Jerchel|first1=Michael|last2=Schnellbacher|first2=Uwe|title=Leopard 2 Main Battle Tank 1979–1998|year=1998|publisher=Osprey|location=New York|isbn=978-1-85532-691-0|pages=17–18}} ===Leopard 2A3=== The fourth batch of 300 vehicles, 165 by Krauss-Maffei (Chassis Nr. 10624 to 10788) and 135 by MaK (Chassis Nr. 20510 to 20644), was delivered between December 1984 and December 1985. The main change was the addition of the SEM80/90 digital radio sets (also being fitted to the Leopard 1 at the same time), and the ammunition reloading hatches being welded shut. Even with these minor changes the new batch was known as the ''2A3''.{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} ===Leopard 2A4=== [[File:Bezoek Hare Majesteit de Koningin aan Nederlandse troep in Seedorf en omstreken , Bestanddeelnr 933-7361.jpg|thumb|right|Early Dutch Leopard 2 tanks in 1986]] The most widespread version of the Leopard 2 family, the 2A4 models included more substantial changes, including an automated fire and explosion suppression system, an all-digital fire control system able to handle new ammunition types, and an improved turret with flat titanium/tungsten armour. The Leopard 2s were manufactured in eight batches between 1985 and 1992. All the older models were upgraded to 2A4 standard. Until 1994, Germany operated a total of 2,125 2A4s (695 newly built and the rest modified older versions),{{citation needed|date=June 2022}} while the Netherlands had an additional 445 tanks. The 2A4 was licensed and manufactured in Switzerland as the '''Panzer 87 "Leopard"''' or '''Pz 87'''. This version included Swiss-built {{cvt|7.5|mm|3}} MG 87 machine guns and communications equipment and featured an improved NBC protection system. Switzerland operated 380 Pz 87 tanks.{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} After 2000, Germany and the Netherlands found themselves with large stocks of tanks that they had no need for after the Cold War. These tanks were sold to NATO or friendly armies around the world. Among these buyers of the surplus tanks were Turkey (purchasing 354 vehicles), Greece (183), Sweden (leased 160), Chile (140), Finland (139), Poland (128), Austria (114), Spain (108), Canada (107), Indonesia (103), Singapore (96), Norway (52), Denmark (51), and Portugal (37).{{cite web|url=http://portal.sipri.org/publications/pages/transfer/trade-register|title=Sipri: Trade Registers|work=sipri.org|access-date=2015-04-01|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140423140358/http://portal.sipri.org/publications/pages/transfer/trade-register|archive-date=2014-04-23}} [[File:Leopard 2A4 Austrian sights.jpg|thumb|upright|An Austrian Leopard 2A4 gunner's sights]] The ''Pz 87WE'' (''WertErhaltung'') is a planned Swiss modification and upgrade of the Pz 87.{{cite news|first=Stefan|last=Liess|title=Leopard 2|date=2007-07-22|publisher=Kampfpanzer.de|url=http://kpz.axlbox.de/servlets/sfs;jsessionid=18966A1AD99684AFF90F809734FBFD8D?s=rquu2hgS7kjI7CT3y&t=/contentManager/selectCatalog&i=1158408897725&b=1158408897725&l=0&e=UTF-8&ParentID=1164791614897&intro=1&CustomerID=0&startRow=0&active=no&cards=1|access-date=2008-04-20|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080420172440/http://kpz.axlbox.de/servlets/sfs|archive-date=2008-04-20}} The modification significantly improves protection through the addition of the Leopard 2A6M's mine protection kit, thicker armour on the front glacis, and a turret equipped with a Swiss-developed armour package using titanium alloy. The turret roof armour is improved and the smoke grenade launchers are redesigned. Further improvements enhance survivability and combat capabilities, such as a turret electric drive similar to the Leopard 2A5, a driver rearview camera, an independent weapons station for the loader, and enhanced command and control systems. The fire control system is upgraded, using the Carl Zeiss Optronics GmbH PERI-R17A2 fire control system. A remote weapons station containing a fully stabilised [[M2 Browning machine gun|Mg 64]] {{cvt|0.5|in|mm}} machine gun is fitted to the tank.{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} The Swiss company RUAG offered an upgrade package for '''Pz 87''' main battle tanks to meet a possible requirement of the Swiss Army for improved protection. It is fitted with a new modular composite armour package. Armour modules can be tailored to provide enhanced protection against a specific threat. Damaged modules can be easily replaced in field conditions. Upgraded tanks are less vulnerable to direct hits, anti-tank missiles, RPG rounds, mines, and IEDs. The vehicle received new sensors such as a sniper detection sensor and a laser warning receiver.{{Cite web|url=http://www.military-today.com/tanks/ruag_leopard_upgrade.htm|title=RUAG Leopard 2 Upgrade - Main battle tank|access-date=2022-06-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220606002935if_/http://www.military-today.com/tanks/ruag_leopard_upgrade.htm|archive-date=2022-06-06|url-status=usurped}}{{cite web|url=https://www.armyrecognition.com/iav_2013_news_coverage_report_pictures_video/ruag_introduces_a_new_leopard_2_a4_armor_upgrade_at_iav_2013_international_armoured_vehicles.html|title=RUAG introduces a new Leopard 2 A4 armor upgrade at IAV 2013 International Armoured Vehicles | IAV 2013 News coverage report pictures video | Defence and security military exhibition 2013|publisher=Armyrecognition.com|date=2013-02-06|access-date=2022-06-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220619042123/https://www.armyrecognition.com/iav_2013_news_coverage_report_pictures_video/ruag_introduces_a_new_leopard_2_a4_armor_upgrade_at_iav_2013_international_armoured_vehicles.html|archive-date=2022-06-19|url-status=dead}} In 2021, the two prototypes with add-on armour were handed to the [[Swiss Military Museum|Militär- und Festungsmuseum Full-Reuenthal]].{{cite web|title=Zwei Schweizer Prototypen des Kampfpanzers Leopard 2|url=https://www.festungsmuseum.ch/zwei-schweizer-prototypen-des-kampfpanzers-leopard-2/|website=Militär- und Festungsmuseum Full-Reuenthal|language=de|access-date=2023-04-05}} [[File:Indonesian Army Leopard tanks.jpg|thumb|Indonesian Leopard 2RIs during a parade]] The Indonesian Army operates the ''Leopard 2 Republic Indonesia'' or ''Leopard 2RI'', an upgraded variant based on Rheinmetall's MBT Revolution upgrade for the Leopard 2A4 tank. The upgrade includes AMAP armour from IBD Deisenroth and Rheinmetall Chempro, improved fire control systems, and battlefield management and situational awareness systems.{{cite web|url=https://armyrecognition.com/may_2016_global_defense_security_news_industry/leopard_2a4_tanks_for_indonesia_will_be_fitted_with_the_revolution_urban_warfare_package_12505163.amp.html|title=Leopard 2A4 tanks for Indonesia will be fitted with the Revolution urban warfare package|website=armyrecognition.com|date=2016-05-25|access-date=2022-04-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130192539/https://armyrecognition.com/may_2016_global_defense_security_news_industry/leopard_2a4_tanks_for_indonesia_will_be_fitted_with_the_revolution_urban_warfare_package_12505163.amp.html|archive-date=2022-11-30|url-status=dead}}{{Cite web|author=ARG|url=http://www.military-today.com/tanks/revolution.htm|title=Revolution - Main battle tank|access-date=2022-06-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220520084318if_/http://www.military-today.com/tanks/revolution.htm|archive-date=2022-05-20|url-status=usurped}} The ''Pz 87–140''{{cite web|url=http://img144.imagevenue.com/img.php?image=13657_pz87_140_122_51lo.jpeg#|title=Pz 87–140 image|access-date=2014-11-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129024533/http://img144.imagevenue.com/img.php?image=13657_pz87_140_122_51lo.jpeg|archive-date=2014-11-29|url-status=live}} is an experimental variant of the Swiss Pz 87 with a {{cvt|140|mm}} gun and additional armour, which was later used on the newer production variants.{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} The ''Leopard 2A4CHL'' is the upgraded Chilean version of the Leopard 2A4 ordered by Chile in 2007. Upgrades include new electronics, sighting, and information systems meant to elevate the Leopard 2A4's networking capability to be equal to that of the Leopard 2A6, a new suspension system, and the upgrading of the tank main gun to the L/55 smoothbore cannon used on the Leopard 2A6. Other upgrades are remote weapon stations over the gunner and commander hatches fitted with the MG3 and [[HK GMG]]. The Leopard 2A4CHL has improved roof and side turret armour and can be uplinked with Chile's battlefield control network.{{Citation needed|date=May 2009}} [[File:MSPO 2012 (18).jpg|thumb|right|A Leopard 2A4 in [[Canadian Army]] configuration, including [[Saab Barracuda]] thermal armour]] [[File:Leopard 2A4 Austria 6.JPG|thumb|right|A Leopard 2A4 of the [[Austrian Armed Forces]]]] The ''[[Leopard 2A4M CAN]]'' is the upgraded Canadian version of the Leopard 2A4 acquired from the Royal Netherlands Army surplus. The Leopard 2A4M CAN is specially designed for the war in Afghanistan, based on experience gained by Leopard 2 operators. The first 20 were delivered in October 2010. Five were deployed to Afghanistan at the end of 2010 and operated until July 2011, when combat operations stopped.{{cite web|url=http://www.defenseindustrydaily.com/tanks-for-the-lesson-leopards-too-for-canada-03208/|access-date=2010-10-12|title=Tanks for the Lesson: Leopards, too, for Canada|work=Defense Industry Daily |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080621072607/http://www.defenseindustrydaily.com/tanks-for-the-lesson-leopards-too-for-canada-03208/%23choices|archive-date=2008-06-21|url-status=live}} Of the other 2A4s acquired, 11 were converted for training use (nine A4s, two A4Ms). In February 2011, Canada bought 12 2A4s/Pz 87 from Switzerland for the 'Force Mobility Enhancement' project which, along with the remaining unused ex-Dutch tanks, saw 18 converted to [[Military engineering vehicle|Armoured Engineering Vehicles]] and 4 converted to [[Armoured Recovery Vehicles]].{{cite web|url=https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/services/procurement/force-mobility-enhancement.html|title=Force mobility enhancement|date=2018-12-13|access-date=2020-11-27}} Canada has also purchased 15 2A4s from Germany as Logistic Stock Vehicles (for spare parts). The ''Leopard 2NG'' (''Next Generation'') is a privately funded Turkish upgrade by [[ASELSAN]] that includes the application of AMAP, upgraded optics, completely overhauled turret mechanics, and a new fire control system on the work since 1995 and to be delivered by late 2011, which is intended to be used on the new Altay MBT. It was developed without an order from the Turkish Army, but might meet the requirements for the modernisation of the Turkish Leopard 2A4s.{{cite web|url=http://www.janes.com/products/janes/defence-security-report.aspx?ID=1065929677&channel=defence&subChannel=land|title=Upgraded Leopard 2 MBT set for firing trials|author=Foss, Christopher|publisher=[[Jane's Information Group]]|access-date=2011-06-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120914173954/http://www.janes.com/products/janes/defence-security-report.aspx?ID=1065929677&channel=defence&subChannel=land|archive-date=2012-09-14|url-status=dead}} The old powerpack and the L/44 gun barrel are kept, but the combat weight is increased to {{cvt|65|t}}. According to Turkish news sources, Finland was interested in getting the Turkish upgrade package to modernise their fleet of Leopard 2A4s. However, in 2015, Finland purchased 120 2A6 vehicles from the Netherlands.{{cite web|url=http://www.radikal.com.tr/Default.aspx?aType=RadikalYazar&ArticleID=1028157&Yazar=MURAT%20YETK%DDN&Date=10.11.2010&CategoryID=98|title=Bakanın ağzından savunma ihalelerinde rüşvet kuşkusu|publisher=Radikal|date=2010-11-09|access-date=2010-12-28}}{{cite web|author=Bakanın ağzından|url=http://www.aktifhaber.com/savunma-ihalelerinde-rusvet-skandali-352580h.htm|title=Savunma İhalelerinde Rüşvet Skandalı 09 Kasım 2010 17:08|publisher=Aktifhaber|date=2009-11-30|access-date=2010-12-28|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101111091245/http://www.aktifhaber.com/savunma-ihalelerinde-rusvet-skandali-352580h.htm|archive-date=2010-11-11}} The Leopard 2 hull was used for the [[Vickers MBT Mark 7|Vickers Mk 7]] main battle tank, which featured a British-designed turret, where some of the innovations later were incorporated into the Challenger 2 design.{{citation needed|date=November 2019}} In December 2015, [[Bumar-Labedy]] signed an agreement with German Rheinmetall Landsysteme Gmbh concerning the technological support of the [[Polish Land Forces#Equipment and modernization|Polish modernisation program for Leopard 2A4 tanks]]. The company will design, document, and execute six prototypes. The first upgraded Leopard 2PLs have arrived in Poland in June 2020, with all 142 tanks to be delivered by 2023.{{cite web|title=Armoured breakthrough|date=2020-05-28|url=https://www.defence24.pl/pancerny-przelom-leopardy-z-gliwic-ida-do-wojska-analiza}} The upgrades include third generation night vision systems (production of the Warsaw PCO), new additional armour modules and anti-splash lining, removal of flammable components (turret drive system and main propulsion system), installation of the new fire protection system, modernisation of the tank's integrated monitoring and testing equipment, the possibility of using new types of ammunition (programmable DM-11 and DM-63), and an auxiliary generator set (APU). Construction of all 142 units will be completed by the end of 2020.{{citation needed|date=December 2019}} Turkey is planning to modernise its Leopard 2A4 MBTs as ''Leopard 2A4TR'' with the T1 Modernisation Package.{{clarify|date=January 2022}} According to the Defence Industry Presidency, Leopard 2A4 tanks will be modernised with; Explosive Reactive Armour (ERA), T1 Reactive-Passive Armour, High Ballistic Strength Cage Armour, Hollow Modular Add-on Armour, Close Range Surveillance System (YAMGÖZ), Laser Warning Receiver System (LIAS), SARP Remote Controlled Weapon System (UKSS), PULAT Active Protection System (AKS), a new power distribution unit, ASELSAN Driver Surveillance System (ADİS) and voice alert system integrations. The modernisation programme is to be completed in two batches. The programme will start with 84 Leopard 2A4 tanks in the first batch and the remaining tanks will be modernised within the 2nd batch. A total of 334 tanks (including prototypes) are planned to be upgraded with the T1 modernisation programme. The new modernised Leopard 2A4 that was presented at the [[BMC (Turkey)|BMC]] factory was fitted with an [[Altay (main battle tank)|Altay]] [[MKE 120 mm tank gun|turret]], which is armed with one {{cvt|120|mm}} 55 calibre smoothbore gun designed and manufactured by the Turkish Company [[Mechanical and Chemical Industry Corporation|MKE]], based on a technology transfer from [[Hyundai Rotem]] of South Korea. A remote-controlled weapon station is mounted on the top of the turret which is armed with a {{cvt|12.7|mm}} calibre heavy machine gun.{{cite 2A4s|date=2021-02-07|access-date=2021-02-07|website=savunmasanayist.com|language=tr}}{{cite
