====Leopard 2A4V==== On 1 September 2023, video on social media showed Ukrainian crews with 30 Leopard 2A4 upgraded with Kontakt [[Reactive armour#Explosive reactive armour|ERA]] and [[T-80|T-80U]] style rubber screens, called "Leopard 2A4V" by observers.{{cite news|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/davidaxe/2023/09/02/30-ukrainian-leopard-2a4-tanks-assembled-in-one-field-a-reminder-that-ukraine-still-has-most-of-its-leopard-2s/|website=forbes.com|title=30 Ukrainian Leopard 2A4 Tanks Assembled In One Field—A Reminder That Ukraine Still Has Most Of Its Leopard 2s|first=David|last=Axe|date=2023-09-02|access-date=2023-09-02}} This followed previous sightings in Ukraine of a Canadian supplied Leopard 2A4 upgraded with [[Kontakt-1]] ERA. ===Leopard 2 Marksman=== {{Main|Marksman anti-aircraft system}} [[File:Kalustoesittely_itsenäisyyspäivä_2015_17_Leopard_2_Marksman.JPG|thumb|A Leopard 2 Marksman of the Finnish Army]]Finland has modernised its Marksman [[SPAAG]] vehicles by replacing the original T-55AM chassis with a newer Leopard 2A4 chassis.{{cite web|url=https://www.hs.fi/kotimaa/art-2000002811544.html|title=Armeija ottaa vanhojen Marksman-vaunujen tykkitornit uuteen käyttöön|last=Huhtanen|first=Jarmo|date=2015-03-25|website=hs.fi|publisher=Helsingin Sanomat|access-date=2015-03-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170419013744/http://www.hs.fi/kotimaa/art-2000002811544.html|archive-date=2017-04-19|url-status=live}} The upgraded Marksman vehicles were scheduled to enter service with the Finnish Army in 2016.{{cite web|url=http://puolustusvoimat.fi/wcm/a2748e00495d6be1a9e0a98833fba23b/Toimintanaytoksen_materiaalitiedot_5+8+2015.pdf?MOD=AJPERES|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151005155147/http://www.puolustusvoimat.fi/wcm/a2748e00495d6be1a9e0a98833fba23b/Toimintanaytoksen_materiaalitiedot_5%2B8%2B2015.pdf?MOD=AJPERES|title=MAAVOIMIEN LIIKKUVUUDEN JA TULIVOIMAN ROLL OUT PANSSARIPRIKAATISSA 5.8.2015 – Esiteltävä kalusto|publisher=Finnish Defence Forces|language=fi|date=2015-08-05|archive-date=2015-10-05|access-date=2017-12-02|url-status=dead}} The new Leopard 2 chassis greatly improves mobility compared to the older T-55AM chassis, both on- and off-road. The Leopard 2 chassis is larger, providing a more stable firing platform for the Marksman turret to operate from.{{cite web|url=http://weaponsystems.net/weaponsystem/EE03%20-%20Marksman.html|title=Marksman|author=|website=weaponsystems.net|access-date=2017-12-02|quote=The Leopard 2 chassis also provides a much increased mobility over the older T-55AM chassis, both on roads and in the field.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170112062530/http://www.weaponsystems.net/weaponsystem/EE03%20-%20Marksman.html|archive-date=2017-01-12|url-status=live}} ===Leopard 2 Imp=== [[File:Leo 2 Imp under strv NY utprovning 1.jpg|thumb|Leopard 2 Improved prototype being tested in Sweden, {{Circa|1993}}]] "Leopard 2 Improved" was a series of three prototypes used to test possible further enhancements beyond the Leopard 2A4 model, developed beginning in 1988.Scheibert (1996), p. 3. After a concept phase, a component test bed (KVT, ''Komponentenversuchsträger'') was built in 1989, followed by two troop trial vehicles (TVM, ''Truppenversuchsmuster''). The Leopard 2 Improved was mostly focused on improving armour protection, introducing the wedge-shaped, spaced add-on armour at the turret front, as well as hull and roof add-on armour, greatly improving protection against hollow charge and kinetic energy threats. It does not form a [[shot trap|shot-trap]], since it does not deflect the penetratours outwards to hit the hull or turret ring. The gun mantlet was redesigned to accept the new armour. Aside of improved armour protection, these tanks also included improved optics, navigation systems and electronics. Following the initial trials of the two TVM prototypes in Germany and an agreement of the Leopard 2 user states, the second TVM prototype was modified (becoming the TVM 2 mod.) by removing several parts such as the add-on hull and roof armour,Scheibert (1996), p. 4 becoming the basis for the Leopard 2A5 model. One Leopard 2 Improved (TVM 2) competed in Sweden against the Leclerc and M1A2 Abrams, leading to the adoption of the Stridsvagn 122. ===Leopard 2A5=== [[File:Polish Leopard 2A5 main battle tank during Strong Europe Tank Challenge 2017.jpg|thumb|right|Leopard 2A5 of the [[Polish Land Forces]], 2017]] The Leopard 2 Improved was developed into the Leopard 2A5. Most of its improvements were focused on armour protection; it was enhanced by adding external add-on modules to the turret and replacing the turret's internal armour modules with ones of newer, improved composition.Scheibert (1996), p. 6 The interior received spall liners to reduce fragments if the armour is penetrated. The commander's sight was moved to a new position behind the hatch and it received an independent thermal channel. The gunner's sight was moved to the turret roof as opposed to the cavity in the front armour in previous models. A heavier sliding driver's hatch was fitted.{{cite book|last1=Jerchel|first1=Michael|last2=Schnellbacher|first2=Uwe|title=Leopard 2 Main Battle Tank 1979–1998|year=1998|publisher=Osprey|location=New York|isbn=978-1-85532-691-0|section=The Improved Leopard 2}} The hydraulic turret drives were replaced by an all-electric system, increasing reliability and crew safety, as well as weight savings. The gun braking system was improved to prepare for the later mounting of the new L/55 gun tube and to enable firing of more powerful ammunition, such as the DM53 APFSDS. The first A5s were handed over to the German army tank school in 1995 and started to enter regular service with Panzerbataillon 33 in December the same year. The Leopard 2A5 DK is a variant of the Leopard 2A5 similar to the Leopard 2A6 with some small modifications, used by the Danish Army.{{cite web|url=https://www2.forsvaret.dk/viden-om/materiel/haerens_materiel/kampvogne/Pages/Kampvogne2.aspx|title=Kampvogne|website=[[forsvaret.dk]]|language=da|access-date=2018-06-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612141030/https://www2.forsvaret.dk/viden-om/materiel/haerens_materiel/kampvogne/Pages/Kampvogne2.aspx|archive-date=2018-06-12|url-status=dead}} ====Stridsvagn 122==== {{Main|Stridsvagn 122}} [[File:Strv122 3 cropped.jpg|thumb|A Stridsvagn 122 of the Swedish Army]] Stridsvagn 122 (also known as ''Leopard 2A5S''{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160807003302/http://www.ointres.se/2011_Lindstrom_IAV_Conference.pdf|title=The Swedish Armoured Fighting Vehicle programmes: "Getting the most from protected platforms as weapon systems"|author=Rickard O. Lindström|archive-date=2016-08-07|url-status=dead|url=http://www.ointres.se/2011_Lindstrom_IAV_Conference.pdf|access-date=2023-10-16}} and ''Leopard 2 "Improved" A5 SE''{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160401205827/http://www.ointres.se/2014-09-18_svensk_stridsfordonsutvecckling.pdf|title=Stridsfordon: Utveckling och anskaffning i Sverige - Arsenalen den 18 september Rickard O. Lindström|author=Rickard O. Lindström|archive-date=2016-04-01|url-status=dead|url=http://www.ointres.se/2014-09-18_svensk_stridsfordonsutvecckling.pdf|access-date=2023-10-16}} ) is a Swedish Army tank based on the Leopard 2 Improved. 120 units were built, 91 of which were licence-produced in Sweden. The tank features increased armour on the turret top and front hull, and improved command-, control- and fire-control systems. Externally, it can be distinguished from the Leopard 2A5 by the French GALIX smoke dispensers, different storage bins, and the much thicker crew hatches.{{cite web|url=http://www.fmv.se/WmTemplates/Page.aspx?id=1106|website=fmv.se|title=Stridsvagn 122|language=sv|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050210213646/http://www.fmv.se/WmTemplates/Page.aspx?id=1106|archive-date=2005-02-10|url-status=dead}} The Strv 122B+ Evolution, a variant equipped with modular AMAP composite armour from IBD Deisenroth, has increased 360° protection against threats like EFPs, RPGs and IEDs.{{cite web|url=http://www.ibd-deisenroth-engineering.de/news/items/MBT122B_with_new_Protection.html?file=tl_files/resources/content-pdfs/2010-12%20New%20MBT122B%20Evolution%20with%20Unprecedented%20Protection.pdf|title=New MBT122B Evolution with Unprecedented Protection|access-date=2010-12-28|publisher=IBD Deisenroth Engineering|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111008032615/http://www.ibd-deisenroth-engineering.de/news/items/MBT122B_with_new_Protection.html?file=tl_files%2Fresources%2Fcontent-pdfs%2F2010-12%20New%20MBT122B%20Evolution%20with%20Unprecedented%20Protection.pdf|archive-date=2011-10-08}} The width of {{convert|4|m}} has been kept, while the weight increases by only {{convert|350|kg}}. ===Leopard 2-140=== In the early 1990s,{{citation needed|date=January 2018}} Rheinmetall began development of a {{cvt|140|mm}} smoothbore cannon for use in future tank designs. The new gun was intended to counter new Soviet tank developments, especially since the next generation of Soviet main battle tanks were rumoured to be armed with a {{cvt|135|mm}} or {{cvt|152|mm}} cannon. The new {{cvt|140|mm}} cannon was part of a modernisation programme for the Leopard 2 known as the KWS III.{{cite web|url=http://www.tanks-encyclopedia.com/coldwar/West_Germany/Leopard-2.php|title=Krauss-Maffei Wegmann Leopard 2 (1978)|author=David.B|date=2015-05-31|website=tanks-encyclopedia.com|access-date=2017-11-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171102173045/http://www.tanks-encyclopedia.com/coldwar/West_Germany/Leopard-2.php|archive-date=2017-11-02|url-status=live}}{{Self-published source|date=January 2018}}{{Unreliable source?|date=January 2018}} Test firing of the new {{cvt|140|mm}} cannon was conducted. Results showed that the gun had high penetration values, and had a muzzle velocity of around 2,000 metres a second, with potential to be increased further. However, the {{cvt|140|mm}} rounds were too heavy for the tank crew to handle effectively.{{citation needed|date=January 2023}} The KWS III upgrade was to feature a new turret. This new turret was equipped with the planned {{cvt|140|mm}} cannon and an autoloader. The introduction of an autoloader reduced the tank's crew to three members, as a dedicated loader was no longer needed. The gun's 32 rounds of ammunition were stored separate from the crew in a large compartment occupying the entire rear of the turret, in order to increase crew survivability in the event of a [[cooking off|cook off]]. The turntable-style turret had the gun offset to the left side, due to the autoloader's lateral feeding of ammunition into the cannon breech.{{citation needed|date=January 2018}} The turret was powered by an electro-hydraulic drive and featured an IFIS [[battlefield management system]]. The crew was protected by an armoured capsule and ballistic protection for the hull was to be improved. The planned protection level of the KWS III upgrade was to be equal to or better than the Leopard 2A5.{{Unreliable source?|date=January 2018}} A total of 650 Leopard 2 KWS III tanks were originally projected to be purchased. However, in 1995, the KWS III programme was cancelled due to {{clarify|text=changes in the political environment.|date=November 2017}} Despite this, development continued on the {{cvt|140|mm}} cannon,{{citation needed|date=January 2018}} with Rheinmetall coordinating with the British [[Royal Ordnance]] and French [[GIAT]] companies.{{citation needed|date=January 2023}} The {{cvt|140|mm}} cannon was fitted to an old Leopard 2 prototype with the turret T19.{{cite book|last1=Hilmes|first1=Rolf|title=Kampfpanzer heute und morgen: Konzepte – Systeme – Technologien|date=2007-11-30|publisher=Motorbuch Verlag|location=Germany|isbn=978-3613027930|page=230|language=de}} Counterweights were added to the rear of the turret to balance the increased weight of the {{cvt|140|mm}} cannon. The modified Leopard 2 was not equipped with any other KWS III upgrades apart from the new gun. Live fire testing showed mixed results, where the {{cvt|140|mm}} cannon showed superior penetrating power compared to the existing {{cvt|120|mm}} cannon, but demonstrated poorer handling characteristics.{{Unreliable source?|date=January 2018}} The lack of the autoloader on the prototype further hampered performance.{{Unreliable source?|date=January 2018}} ===Leopard 2A6=== [[File:Leo2A6M li.jpg|thumb|A German Leopard 2A6M with turret reversed]] The Leopard 2A6 includes the addition of the [[Rheinmetall Rh-120#Rh-120 L/55 120mm|Rheinmetall {{cvt|120|mm}} L/55]] smoothbore gun and other changes. All German tank battalions of the "crisis intervention forces" are equipped with the A6. Canada purchased twenty Leopard 2A6s from the Netherlands. These were delivered in 2007. Portugal purchased 37 Leopard 2A6s from the Dutch in 2007, with delivery in 2008. In January 2014, Finland purchased 100 L2A6s, as well as munitions, simulators, and a ten-year supply of reserve parts from the Netherlands. The tanks were delivered in batches between 2015 and 2019.{{cite web|url=http://yle.fi/uutiset/finland_in_200_million-euro_used_tank_deal_with_the_netherlands/7035576|title=Finland in 200 million-euro used tank deal with the Netherlands|date=2014-01-16|access-date=2014-01-16|publisher=Yle|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140116193831/http://yle.fi/uutiset/finland_in_200_million-euro_used_tank_deal_with_the_netherlands/7035576|archive-date=2014-01-16|url-status=live}} The Leopard 2A6A1 is a command version of the Leopard 2A6, stemming from the KWS I programme. The vehicle includes additional radios (with the number depending on the level of command) to accommodate the communications for section, platoon, troop, company, squadron or battalion commanders. For section leaders, the vehicle is fitted with 1x SEM 80 and 1x SEM 90 VHF radios. For platoon or troop commanders, the vehicle is fitted with 1x SEM 80 and 1x SEM 90 VHF radios along with an 800m field telephone cable drum fitted at the rear of the vehicle. For company, squadron or battalion commanders the vehicle is fitted with 2x SEM 80 or 1x SEM 93 and 1x SEM 90 VHF radios along with an {{cvt|800|m}} field telephone cable drum, for either fitted at the rear of the vehicle.{{cite book|last1=|first1=|title=Janes Land Warfare Platforms: Armoured Fighting Vehicles - Tracked 2020-2021|year=2020|publisher=Jane's Information Group|page=99|isbn=9780710633446}} The Leopard 2A6M is a version of the 2A6 with enhanced mine protection under the chassis, and internal enhancements to improve crew survivability.{{cite journal|last=Foss|first=Christopher F.|date=2007-08-08|title=Canada receives first upgraded Leopard 2A6M MBT|journal=[[Jane's Defence Weekly]]|volume=44|issue=32|page=10|issn=0265-3818|oclc=210556835|id=BL Shelfmark 4646.840000}} In the summer of 2007, Canada borrowed 20 A6Ms from Germany for deployment to Afghanistan. [[File:Leopard 2A6 HEL (2).jpg|thumb|A [[Hellenic Army]] Leopard 2A6HEL]] The Leopard 2 HEL ("[[Hellenes|Hellenic]]") is a derivative of the 2A6 export variant, "2A6EX" with additional customisation to meet the Greek needs. It has supplemental reinforcements on the upper [[Glacis|glacis plate]] and crew hatches, as well as a full [[MEXAS]] package. Tactically and technically it is integrated with the NATO-interoperable INIOCHOS command and information system, as well as, a laser rangefinder and thermal imaging devices.{{cite web|last=Gao|first=Charlie|date=2021-11-10|title=These Are the 5 Tanks Ready to Defend NATO|url=https://nationalinterest.org/blog/reboot/these-are-5-tanks-ready-defend-nato-195956|access-date=2024-04-23|website=The National Interest}}{{cite web|url=http://army.gr/el/organosi/oplika-systimata/leo-2hel|title=LEO 2HEL|access-date=2024-04-24|publisher=Hellenic Army General Staff|language=el|archive-date=19 April 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220419185317/http://army.gr/el/organosi/oplika-systimata/leo-2hel|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.defense-aerospace.com/rheinmetall-to-upgrade-greek-army-leopard-2-tanks/|title=Major Order: Rheinmetall to Supply Electronics for Hellenic Army Leopard 2 Tanks|date=2006-09-14|access-date=2024-04-24|website=Defence-aerospace.com}} It was ordered by the Greek Army in 2003 (in a package together with Leopard 1A5s) for 1.7 billion [[€]], with 170 tanks delivered between 2006 and 2009. A total of 140 were built in Greece by [[Hellenic Vehicle Industry|ELBO]], which delivered the first units in late 2006. They entered service with the [[Hellenic Army]] in 2008.{{cite web|url=http://greekmilitary.net/greekmbtanks.htm|title=Leopard 2 HEL images and info|access-date=2008-07-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080516162723/http://greekmilitary.net/greekmbtanks.htm|archive-date=2008-05-16|url-status=live}}{{cite web|date=2020-08-25|title=Leopard 2 Main Battle Tank|url=https://www.army-technology.com/projects/leopard/|access-date=2024-04-23|website=Army Technology|quote=In March 2003, the Hellenic Army of Greece ordered 170 Leopard 2 HEL (a version of the 2A6EX). The first 30 are being assembled by KMW, with the remainder by ELBO of Greece. The first locally built tank was delivered in October 2006. The Leopard 2A6 HEL entered service with the Hellenic Army in May 2008.}} The Leopard 2A6M CAN is a Canadian variant of the Leopard 2A6M. Significant modifications include distinctive black boxes mounted on the rear of the turret bustle,{{cite web|url=https://www.sfu.ca/casr/ft-leopard-2a6m-can.htm|title=The First of Twenty Loaned Leopard 2A6M CAN Arrive in Kandahar: A Glimpse of the CF's Future (With a Little Help From Our Friends)|access-date=2008-07-06|publisher=[[Canadian American Strategic Review]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080418075012/http://www.sfu.ca/casr/ft-leopard-2a6m-can.htm|archive-date=2008-04-18|url-status=dead}} and stand-off [[slat armour]].{{cite web|url=https://www.sfu.ca/casr/bg-leopard2-netherlands.htm#2a6m|title=CASR Background — CF Leased & Purchased Leopard 2 A6M / 2 A4 Tanks|access-date=2008-07-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080416165407/http://www.sfu.ca/casr/bg-leopard2-netherlands.htm#2a6m|archive-date=2008-04-16|url-status=dead}} The first tanks configured in this variant were 20 loaned from the German Bundeswehr in an effort to increase firepower and protection given to Canadian troops operating in the south of Afghanistan. The loaned tanks retain their German MG3 machine guns, the ex-Dutch tanks are also expected to retain their FN MAG machine guns due to commonality with Canadian stocks of C6 GPMG, itself a variant of the FN MAG.{{cite web|url=https://www.sfu.ca/casr/bg-leopard2-afghan.htm|title=CASR Background — Leopard 2 A6M / 2 A4 Tanks for the Canadian Forces?|access-date=2008-07-06|publisher=[[Canadian American Strategic Review]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080416181639/http://www.sfu.ca/casr/bg-leopard2-afghan.htm|archive-date=2008-04-16|url-status=dead}} Due to the loaned status of the first twenty tanks, the air conditioning unit originally could not be installed, as only minimal changes could be made. The crew wore cooling vests instead, and the turret's electric drive generates less heat than the hydraulic drive of the older Leopard C2. The loaned German tanks will be kept by the Canadian Forces and may be further upgraded, while ex-Dutch Leopard 2A6s were modified to German Leopard 2A6M specifications and used as restitution for the loaned tanks.{{cite news|title=Letter of Interest: Tank Replacement Project|date=2008-03-19|work=MERX|publisher=Government of Canada|url=http://www.merx.com/English/SUPPLIER_Menu.Asp?WCE=Show&TAB=1&PORTAL=MERX&State=7&id=PW-%24%24BL-225-16850&FED_ONLY=0&hcode=pdldErIx17TWSULPr3KQEg%3d%3d|access-date=2008-04-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080609232922/http://www.merx.com/English/SUPPLIER_Menu.Asp?WCE=Show&TAB=1&PORTAL=MERX&State=7&id=PW-%24%24BL-225-16850&FED_ONLY=0&hcode=pdldErIx17TWSULPr3KQEg%3D%3D|archive-date=2008-06-09|url-status=dead}} Canadian Leopard 2s in Afghanistan were later fitted with air conditioning units, a much-needed commodity in the scorching desert of Afghanistan, and [[Saab Group|Saab]]'s Barracuda camouflage mats, which reduce solar loading by 50 percent.{{cite web|url=http://www.casr.ca/101-army-armour-leopard-2a6m.htm|title=Canadian Forces Armour — Leopard 2A6M CAN Main Battle Tank|access-date=2010-05-11|publisher=[[Canadian American Strategic Review]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100627144153/http://www.casr.ca/101-army-armour-leopard-2a6m.htm|archive-date=2010-06-27}} The Leopard 2A6TR was the Turkish variant during the Turkish Army tank procurement project in 2000. The version was based on 2A6EX. The project was dropped in favor of developing the indigenous [[Altay (main battle tank)|Altay]].{{cite web|url=https://www.savunmasanayist.com/tank-2000den-altaya-turkiyenin-tank-seruveni/|title=Tank 2000'den ALTAY'a Türkiye'nin tank serüveni|date=2020-02-18|language=tr}} ====Leopardo 2E==== {{Main|Leopard 2E}} [[File:Leopardo 2E. zaragoza 1.jpg|thumb|Spanish Leopard 2E]]The Leopard 2E is a derivative of the 2A6, with greater armour protection,{{cite magazine|last=Candil|first=Antonio J.|date=2007-02-01|title=The Spanish Leopard 2E: A Magnificent Tool|magazine=Military Technology|publisher=Mönch Editorial Group|location=Bonn|page=66|volume=31|issue=2}} developed under a programme of co-production between the defence industries of Spain and Germany. The programme was developed within the frame of collaboration decided in 1995 between the Defence Ministries of both countries, which also included the cession of use by period of five years of 108 Leopard 2A4 from the German Army to the Spanish Army. The session was extended up to 2016, and after that those tanks will be the sole property of the Spanish Army, as has been made public in January 2006, then having been paid a total of €15,124,014 in ten yearly installments, giving the Spanish co-ownership from 2006. In 1998, the Spanish government agreed to locally build 219 tanks of the Leopard 2E line, 16 recovery tanks of Leopard 2ER (Buffalo), and 4 training vehicles. They chose Santa Bárbara Sistemas as the main contractor. The programme, with a budget of €1,939.4 million, includes integrated logistical support, training courses for crew instructors and maintenance engineers, and driving, turret, maintenance, aiming, and shooting simulators. Deliveries of the first batch began in 2004.{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} === Leopard 2PL === {{Main|Leopard 2PL}} [[File:Leopard 2PL - Szkolenie Wojska Polskiego w Nowej Dębie (cropped).jpg|thumb|A Leopard 2PL]]The Leopard 2PL is a Polish modernised version of the Leopard 2A4, carried out in cooperation with Rheinmetall and the [[Polish Armaments Group]] ({{langx|pl|Polska Grupa Zbrojeniowa, PGZ}}). The Leopard 2PL MBT is primarily tasked with assault, maintaining territory, and supporting mechanised and motorised subdivisions with its onboard weapon systems in all weather conditions during the day and night. The main upgrades when compared to the Leopard 2A4 include modernisation of the commander's and gunner's sight, additional ballistic modules on the turret, replacement of the hydraulic stabilisation system with a new electric system, and new fire extinguishing and fire suppression systems.{{cite web|title=Bumar Leopard 2PL MBT|url=https://bumar.gliwice.pl/en/strefa-militarna/o/modernizacja-czolgow-leopard-2a4|access-date=2020-07-09|website=bumar.gliwice.pl|language=pl}} The upgrade included a new commander's control and monitoring system, the installation of an auxiliary power unit (APU), a new turret stowage compartment for crew equipment, the modernisation of its main gun to use new types of programmable ammunition, and the integration of day/night rear camera for drivers. Included are customised towing vehicles due to the increased weight of the upgraded tank.{{cite web|title=Breakthrough. Polish Army Takes Delivery of Leopard 2PL Tanks - Defence24.com|url=https://defence24.com/breakthrough-polish-army-takes-delivery-of-leopard-2pl-tanks|access-date=2020-07-09|website=defence24.com|date=2020-05-29}} The upgraded 2PL version is in service with the [[Polish Land Forces]]. Of the Leopard 2A4s from the first (128) and the second (14) batches, 24 have been upgraded to Leopard 2PL standard.{{cite web|url=http://polska-zbrojna.pl/home/articleshow/27196?t=Pierwsze-Leopardy-2PL-juz-w-Polsce#|title=Pierwsze Leopardy 2PL już w Polsce|publisher=Polska-zbrojna.pl|access-date=2020-01-17|language=pl|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190624125547/http://www.polska-zbrojna.pl/home/articleshow/27196?t=Pierwsze-Leopardy-2PL-juz-w-Polsce|archive-date=2019-06-24|url-status=live}} The rest will be upgraded to the 2PLM1 standard.{{cite web|url=https://zbiam.pl/wojsko-polskie-prezentuje-zmodernizowane-czolgi/|title=Wojsko Polskie prezentuje zmodernizowane czołgi|first=Patriota|last=pisze|language=pl|date=2020-09-09|website=Wydawnictwo militarne ZBIAM}} ===Leopard 2 PSO=== [[File:Leo2pso 009.jpg|thumb|A Leopard 2 PSO at Eurosatory 2006]] The new Leopard 2 PSO (Peace Support Operations) variant is designed especially for [[urban warfare]], which had been encountered in peacekeeping operations with increasing frequency. The Leopard 2 PSO is equipped with more effective all-around protection, a secondary weapons station, improved reconnaissance ability, an obstacle clearance blade (OCB), a shorter gun barrel for manoeuvring on urban streets at the expense of fire range, non-lethal armament, close-range surveillance ability through camera systems, a searchlight and further changes to improve its perseverance and mobility in built-up non-wide open areas. These features are similar to the [[Tank Urban Survival Kit]] for the American M1A2 Abrams.{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} The vehicle was purely a tech demonstrator, which eventually lead to the development of the Leopard 2A7+.{{cite web|url=https://fighting-vehicles.com/tanks/leopard-2-tank/|title=Leopard 2 Tank|Comprehensive vehicle history & operator details|website=fighting-vehicles.com|access-date=2024-08-27}} ===Leopard 2A7=== The Leopard 2A7 vehicle is not intended to be optimised for combat in urban terrain, thus it is fundamentally different from the KMW variant, the: ''2A7+'' (see below). A total of 20 vehicles were provided for converting. It involves former Dutch A6NL models returned by Canada to Germany. The original upgrade to A6M has been extended in coordination with Canada and includes a crew-compartment cooling-system from the Leopard 2 A6M-HEL series, a new {{cvt|20|kW}} auxiliary power unit based on the Steyr Motors M12 TCA UI engine,{{cite web|url=http://www.kmweg.com/fileadmin/user_upload/pdfs/Press_Releases/2016/Press_release_en_EUROSATORY_2016.pdf|title=The LEOPARD 2 A7V|publisher=Krauss-Maffei Wegmann GmbH & Co. KG|access-date=2016-11-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161120213553/http://www.kmweg.com/fileadmin/user_upload/pdfs/Press_Releases/2016/Press_release_en_EUROSATORY_2016.pdf|archive-date=2016-11-20|url-status=dead}} the Saab Barracuda Mobile Camouflage System (MCS) with Heat-Transfer Reduction (HTR CoolCam) system,{{cite web|url=http://saab.com/land/signature-management/platform-integrated-systems/mcs_mobile_camouflage_system/|title=MCS Mobile Camouflage System|website=Saab Solutions|language=en-US|access-date=2016-11-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161120215408/http://saab.com/land/signature-management/platform-integrated-systems/mcs_mobile_camouflage_system/|archive-date=2016-11-20|url-status=dead}} a field trial proven combat management and information system (IFIS: ''Integriertes Führungs- und Informationssystem''), onboard network optimisation with ultracapacitors in the chassis and turret, a SOTAS IP digital intercom system, a renewal of the fire suppression system in the crew compartment, and the retrofitting of Attica thermal imaging module in the commander optics. The weapon system is adapted for firing HE ammunition. It is fitted for, but not with, additional passive side protection armour. The first Leopard 2A7 was handed over to the German Army in Munich in December 2014. 14 vehicles were produced for [[Tank Battalion 203]], 4 went to the [[Armoured Corps Training Centre (Germany)|Armoured Corps Training Centre]] and one vehicle went to the Technical School for Land Systems and School for Technology of the Army. The last tank remains as a reference vehicle at KMW.{{cite web|url=http://www.janes.com/article/46904/germany-receives-first-leopard-2a7-mbt|title=Germany receives first Leopard 2A7 MBT|access-date=2014-12-22|publisher=IHS Jane's Defence Weekly|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150501043922/http://www.janes.com/article/46904/germany-receives-first-leopard-2a7-mbt|archive-date=2015-05-01|url-status=dead}} The Leopard 2A7V (The V stands for "verbessert" which is German for improved) is a variant of the Leopard 2A7 which is currently in-service the Bundeswehr. It features improved cameras for the commander and gunner. In addition, the rear view camera for the driver is added. The 120mm barrel has been hardened, allowing the ability to fire more modern extended-range ammunition, increasing effective range up to 5,000 metres. Another thing is the Battle Management System feature for digital electronics have been added, allowing better coordination with friendly forces. Next, the chassis have been additionally reinforced by an additional protection module at the front to counteract armour-piercing ammunition, to make up for the increase weight of the additional armour, it is equipped with an improved/more powerful drive system and drive train.{{Cite web |title=Leopard 2 A7V main battle tank |url=https://www.bundeswehr.de/en/organization/army/mission/vjtf-2023/leopard-2-a7v-main-battle-tank |access-date=January 17, 2025 |website=Bundeswehr}} The Danish Armed Forces received its first Leopard 2A7 main battle tanks upgraded in Germany from the Leopard 2A5DK version at the Dragoon Barracks in Holstebro. The Danish Army will receive a total of 44 Leopard 2A7 vehicles by 2022.{{cite web|url=https://militaryleak.com/2020/02/08/royal-danish-army-receives-first-leopard-2a7-main-battle-tank/|title=Royal Danish Army Receives First Leopard 2A7V Main Battle Tank|website=militaryleak.com|date=2020-02-08}} Siemon T. Wezeman, senior researcher at SIPRI's arms transfers and military expenditure programme, stated that information from the UN Register of Conventional Arms 2016, indicated that some Leopard 2A7s were transferred to Singapore after 2014. SIPRI reported that the Singapore Army probably acquired a total of 45 Leopard 2A7s between 2016 and 2019, but the Singapore's Ministry of Defence denied having acquired the 2A7 version, presumably to minimise anxiety among her neighbours.{{cite web|last=Yeo|first=Mike|date=2019-02-25|title=German documents reveal Singapore received more Leopard 2 tanks|url=https://www.defensenews.com/land/2019/02/21/german-documents-reveal-singapore-received-more-leopard-2-tanks/|access-date=2021-08-06|website=Defense News|language=en-US}}{{cite web|last=Yeo|first=Mike|date=2018-03-20|title=Singapore denies acquisition of new Leopard tank variant|url=https://www.defensenews.com/global/asia-pacific/2018/03/20/singapore-denies-acquisition-of-new-leopard-tank-variant/|access-date=2021-08-06|website=Defense News|language=en-US}}{{cite web|title=Singapore allegedly acquires Leopard 2A7 tanks – Shephard Media|url=https://www.shephardmedia.com/news/landwarfareintl/singapore-allegedly-acquires-leopard-2a7-tanks/|date=2018-03-20|access-date=2021-08-06|website=shephardmedia.com}} In February 2023, Norway ordered 54 Leopard 2A7 tanks to be delivered from 2026, with a further option for 18 vehicles if necessary.{{cite news|title=Tyske Leopard 2A7 blir Norges nye stridsvogn|url=https://www.tv2.no/nyheter/innenriks/tyske-leopard-2a7-blir-norges-nye-stridsvogn/15467364/|date=2023-02-03|publisher=TV2|access-date=2023-02-03|language=no}} This order was later changed into a newly specified 2A8 NOR sub-variant of the 2A8. ===Leopard 2A7+=== [[File:Leopard 2 A7, Eurosatory 2010.jpg|thumb|A Leopard 2A7+ at Eurosatory 2010]] The Leopard 2A7+ was first shown to the public during the [[Eurosatory|Eurosatory 2010]], featuring the label "Developed by KMW – tested and qualified by the German Ministry of Defence". The Leopard 2A7+ has been tested by the Bundeswehr under the name ''UrbOp'' (urban operations).{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} The Leopard 2A7+ is designed to operate both in [[low-intensity conflict|low-intensity]] and high-intensity conflicts.{{cite web|url=http://www.kmweg.de/2922-bD1lbiZuZXdzX2lkPTQzMDAx-~rechte-navi~pressemitteilungen~news_detail.html|title=German success story continues – the new LEOPARD 2 A7+|website=Krauss-Maffei Wegmann|date=2010-06-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100627160134/http://www.kmweg.de/2922-bD1lbiZuZXdzX2lkPTQzMDAx-~rechte-navi~pressemitteilungen~news_detail.html|archive-date=2010-06-27|url-status=dead}} about the Leopard 2A7 +. The tank's protection has been increased by modular armour. The frontal protection has been improved with a dual kit on the turret and hull front, while 360° protection against [[rocket propelled grenade|RPGs]] and mine protection increase the survivability of the tank in urban operations. The modular armour's system components were first used by Canada in Afghanistan.{{cite web|url=http://www.kmweg.com/home/tracked-vehicles/main-battle-tanks/leopard-2-a7/product-information.html|title=Product Information – KMW|website=www.kmweg.com|access-date=2017-03-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170516212527/http://www.kmweg.com/home/tracked-vehicles/main-battle-tanks/leopard-2-a7/product-information.html|archive-date=2017-05-16|url-status=dead}} It can fire programmable [[High Explosive]] munitions. The turret-mounted MG3 has been replaced with a stabilised [[FLW remote weapon station|FLW 200]] [[Remote weapon system|remotely controlled weapon station]]. Mobility, sustainability, and [[situational awareness]] have also been improved. In December 2018, Hungary ordered forty-four 2A7+s (sub-variant 2A7HU), making them the second operator of the improved version, after Qatar. ===Leopard 2A8=== [[File:LEOPARD 2A9.jpg|thumb|A Leopard 2A8 demonstrator at Eurosatory 2022]] The Leopard 2A8 will be based on the current Leopard 2A7HU production model but feature additional improvements; among them the integration of the [[Trophy (countermeasure)|Trophy]] [[active protection system]] and an all-round situational awareness system with sensor-fusion capability. ====Orders==== To replace the eighteen Leopard 2A6 tanks handed over to the Armed Forces of Ukraine, the German Ministry of Defence begun planning a purchase a batch of eighteen Leopard 2A8 tanks (with the option for a further 105) in May 2023.{{cite web|last1=Heiming|first1=Gerhard|title=Rahmenvertrag für bis zu 128 Leopard 2A8 unterschrieben|url=https://esut.de/2023/05/meldungen/42279/rahmenvertrag-fuer-bis-zu-123-leopard-2a8-unterschrieben/|website=Europäische Sicherheit & Technik|date=2023-05-25|publisher=Mittler Report|access-date=2024-01-23}} In July 2024, Germany's budget committee approved a purchase of the remaining 105 tanks, in a contract worth 2.93 bln €. Deliveries are planned between 2027 and 2030 and some ordered tanks will be used by the [[Structure of the German Army#45th Panzer Brigade|45th Panzer Brigade]], which, at the time of purchase, was deployed in Lithuania.{{cite web|title=Germany to order 105 Leopard 2A8 tanks|url=https://mil.in.ua/en/news/germany-to-order-105-leopard-2a8-tanks/|publisher=Militarny|date=2024-07-04|access-date=2024-07-05}} The Czech Ministry of Defence started negotiations for the purchase of 70–77 Leopard 2A8 in May 2023, including domestic manufacturing rights for aspects of the tank production.{{cite web|title=Panzer bonanza: Czech Republic joins Berlin's Leopard upgrade push|url=https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/2023/05/24/panzer-bonanza-czech-republic-joins-berlins-leopard-upgrade-push/|website=Defense News|last=Sprenger|first=Sebastian|date=2023-05-24}}{{cite web|title=Minister Černochová: We Perceive the Biggest Threats of the Present in the Same Way as Germany|url=https://www.defense-aerospace.com/czechia-plans-to-order-77-leopard-2a8-tanks-for-2027-delivery/|publisher=Defense Aerospace|date=2023-07-24}} Czech government approved the purchase in June 2024, with the final order being for 77 tanks delivered by 2030, for an estimated 52 billion Czech crowns.{{cite web|title=Czech government approves plan to buy up to 77 Leopard tanks|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/czech-government-approves-plan-buy-up-77-leopard-tanks-2024-06-12/|publisher=[[Reuters]]|date=2024-06-12|access-date=2024-07-05}} In July 2023 [[Ministry of National Defence (Lithuania)|Lithuanian MoD]] announced that the Leopard 2A8 proved to be the only tank to meet the requirements set by the ministry, leading to the rejection of bids of the [[M1 Abrams]] and [[K2 Black Panther]] tanks.{{cite web|title=German Leopard 2 tank beats Abrams and Black Panther in Lithuania|url=https://defence-industry.eu/german-leopard-2-tank-beats-abrams-and-black-panther-in-lithuania/|publisher=Defence Industry Europe|date=2023-07-26|access-date=2024-07-05}} In January 2024 [[Lithuania]]n State Defence Council agreed to purchase the tanks and associated support vehicles to equip a [[Battalion|Tank Battalion]], but the final cost and the number of vehicles remained a subject of negotiations.{{cite web|title=Lithuania seeks to buy Leopard 2 tanks from Germany|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/lithuania-seeks-buy-leopard-2-tanks-germany-2024-01-23/|website=[[Reuters]]|date=2024-01-23|access-date=2024-07-05}}{{cite web|title=Lithuania's State Defence Council agrees to buy German Leopard tanks – adviser|publisher=[[LRT televizija]]|url= https://www.lrt.lt/en/news-in-english/19/2177909/lithuania-s-state-defence-council-agrees-to-buy-german-leopard-tanks-adviser|date=2024-01-23|access-date=2024-07-05}} In December 2024 Lithuania signed a confirmation of 44 Leopard 2A8 tanks acquisition contract. On 12 July 2023 Italian government confirmed during a Parliament audition that Italy intends to purchase up to 250 Leopard 2A8 tanks from 2023 to 2025.{{cite web|url=https://www.camera.it/leg19/824?tipo=A&anno=2023&mese=07&giorno=12&view=filtered_scheda&commissione=04#/|publisher=Italian Parliament|date=2023-07-12|work=XIX Legislatura|title=Lavori - Resoconti delle Giunte e Commissioni|language=it}} Procurement was completed on 21 February 2024, resulting in the final order of 132 Leopard 2A8 tanks and 130 other vehicles for a total of 8.5 billion € with the deliveries scheduled to be completed by 2037.{{cite web|title=Italian Parliament approves Leopard 2A8 procurement programme|url=https://defence-industry.eu/italian-parliament-approves-leopard-2a8-procurement-programme/|publisher=Defence Industry Europe|date=2024-02-24|access-date=2024-07-05}} In August 2023 Dutch MoD begun planning a procurement of up to 52 Leopard 2A8 tanks in addition to their eighteen leased Leopard 2A6 tanks.{{cite web|publisher=Oryx spioenkop|url=https://www.oryxspioenkop.com/2023/08/high-on-defence-listing-dutch-arms.html|title=High on Defence: Listing Dutch Arms Acquisitions|date=2023-08-27}} This planned acquisition is part of the nation's effort to rebuild their army after severe budget cuts of the 21st century. In February 2024 it came out that the Dutch budget for 2024 did not allocate any funding for the purchase.{{cite web|title=Limits: Netherlands' ambition for Leopard 2A8 battalion hindered|url=https://bulgarianmilitary.com/2024/02/11/limits-netherlands-ambition-for-leopard-2a8-battalion-hindered/|publisher=Bulgarian Military Industry Review|first1=Boyko|last1=Nikolov|date=2024-02-11|access-date=2024-07-05}} In early September 2024 the new government announced that an undefined number of Leopard 2A8 tanks would be ordered. This is now possible because of the new government allocated additional funding exceeding 2% of their GDP. In December 2024, Lithuania signed a contract to acquire 44 Leopard 2A8 tanks from KNDS Germany for €950 million.{{Cite web |date=2024-12-30 |title=Lithuania Buys Cutting-Edge Leopard 2A8 Tanks for €950M and Establishes First Tank Brigade Near Belarus |url=https://www.grosswald.org/lithuania-orders-eu950m-leopard-2a8-tanks-for-first-tank-brigade-near-belarus/ |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=Großwald - Curated News on Geopolitics and Defense |language=en}} This deal provides Lithuania's newly established tank brigade—its first since regaining independence in 1991. The procurement was finalised alongside an agreement to station a German Army brigade within Lithuanian territory by 2027, aligning logistics and maintenance efforts with NATO standards in the Baltic region. The procured main battle tanks are confirmed to feature Trophy APS{{Cite web |date=2024-11-07 |title=Leopard 2 A7A1 MBT Upgraded with APS Trophy Missile Defense |url=https://www.grosswald.org/leopard-2-a7a1-mbt-now-with-trophy-aps-intercept-missiles-within-milliseconds/ |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=Großwald - Curated News on Geopolitics and Defense |language=en}} and next-generation digitalised systems. In January 2025 it was announced that Sweden had signed a deal with [[KNDS Deutschland]] worth $1.97 billion for the purchase of 44 Leopard 2A8s and the upgrading of 66 Strv 122s with deliveries lasting since 2028 till 2031.{{cite web|title=Limits: Sweden bolsters defense with 44 new Leopard 2A8 battle tanks, upgrades to CV90s|url=https://breakingdefense.com/2025/01/sweden-bolsters-defense-with-44-new-leopard-2a8-battle-tanks-upgrades-to-cv90s/|publisher=Breaking Defence|first1=Jonas|last1=Olsson|date=2025-01-09|access-date=2025-01-09}} ====Leopard 2A8 NOR==== The Norwegian armed forces' order of fifty-four Leopard 2A7NOs was changed into a new 2A8 NOR variant by the middle of June 2023. A variety of Norwegian changes and alterations necessitated the renaming of the original 2A7NO into a unique new 2A8 NOR variant. This sub-variant mainly differs from the German 2A8 by integrating a Norwegian-designed C4IS-solution that includes Kongsberg's ICS/CORTEX-solution and Teleplan Globe's FACNAV and NorBMS battlefield management systems.{{cite news|title=Norges nye stridsvogner blir Leopard 2A8 med israeldsignet aktiv beskyttelse|url=https://www.tu.no/artikler/norges-nye-stridsvogner-blir-leopard-2a8-med-israelskdesignet-aktiv-beskyttelse/532729|date=2023-06-17|publisher=TU.no|access-date=2023-06-17|language=no}} ===Leopard 2 A-RC 3.0=== [[File:KNDS Leopard 2 RC3.0 front Klietz 2025.JPG|thumb|Leopard 2A-RC 3.0 prototpe on static display at the [[Klietz]] training area]] Variant presented in June 2024 at the Eurosatory exhibition. It is equipped with an unmanned turret armed with a {{cvt|120|mm}} smoothbore gun fed by a modular linear autoloader, the {{cvt|120|mm}} gun can be exchanged for a {{cvt|130|mm}} or {{cvt|140|mm}} gun, the auto loader is capable of loading 3 rounds in 10 seconds. Its secondary armament consists of a RWCS{{Clarify|reason=RWCS? Rugby World Cup Sevens?|date=November 2024}} armed with a 30x113mm cannon capable of countering drone threats and an anti-tank missile. The weapon suite can be configured for 3D line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) engagement. For its protection, it has a proven active protection system and smoke grenade launcher. It weighs less than {{cvt|60|t}}, measures {{cvt|7.95|m}}, extending to {{cvt|11.17|m}} with the barrel, {{cvt|3.77|m}} wide and {{cvt|2.44|m}} high to the roof of the turret. Its engine generates {{cvt|1500|hp}}, allowing the tank to move at a speed of {{cvt|65|kph}} and its autonomy is {{cvt|460|km}}. It has a crew of 3 men, commander, driver and gunner, all located inside the chassis.{{cite web|url=https://www.armyrecognition.com/news/army-news/army-news-2024/eurosatory-2024-knds-launches-leopard-2-a-rc-3-0-main-battle-tank-with-modular-autoloader|title=Eurosatory 2024: KNDS launches Leopard 2 A-RC 3.0 main battle tank with modular autoloader|website=armyrecognition.com|date=2024-06-17}}{{cite web|url=https://defence-industry.eu/knds-deutschland-introduces-leopard-2-a-rc-3-0-main-battle-tank/|title=KNDS Deutschland introduces Leopard 2 A-RC 3.0 main battle tank|website=Defense Industry Europe|date=2024-06-13}} ===Engineering and driver training derivatives=== ==== Bergepanzer BPz3 Büffel ==== {{Main|{{ill|BPz3 Büffel|lt=BPz3 Büffel|de|Bergepanzer Büffel}}}} [[File:Bergepanzer Bueffel.jpg|thumb|A BPz3 "Büffel", German Army]] The BPz3 [[armoured recovery vehicle]] includes both a [[bulldozer]] and a [[crane (machine)|crane]] with integral [[winch]], allowing it to approach damaged vehicles, even over rough and fought-over terrain, and tow them to safety. It is equipped with a [[machine gun]] for local self-defence, a smoke [[grenade launcher]], and NBC protection. Like the tank, it is powered by a {{cvt|1500|PS|hp kW}} [[diesel engine]]. It is in service with Germany (where it is also designated ''Büffel'' or ''Bergepanzer 3'' for Salvage Tank 3), the Netherlands with 25 vehicles (who co-developed it with Germany and calls it ''Buffel''), Canada, Greece, Singapore (where it is called ''L2-ARV'' locally), Spain (where it is called ''Leopard 2ER Búfalo''), Sweden (in modified form as the ''Bärgningsbandvagn 120; Bgbv 120'') and Switzerland (''BPz3'').{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} ==== WiSENT 2 ==== {{main|{{ill|WiSENT 2|lt=WiSENT 2 ARV|de|WiSENT 2}}}} A multi-purpose, Leopard 2–based Armoured Support Vehicle developed by [[Flensburger Fahrzeugbau]]. The vehicle's modular design allows it to be converted quickly from an Armoured Recovery Vehicle (ARV) to an Armoured Engineer Vehicle (AEV) in less than five hours.{{cite web|url=http://www.ffg-flensburg.de/en/heavy-tracked-vehicles/arv-aev-wisent-2/|title=ARV/AEV Wisent 2|access-date=2014-12-31|publisher=[[Flensburger Fahrzeugbau]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150926025418/http://www.ffg-flensburg.de/en/heavy-tracked-vehicles/arv-aev-wisent-2/|archive-date=2015-09-26|url-status=dead}} ==== AEV 3 Kodiak ==== {{main|AEV 3 Kodiak}} [[File:AEV3 5.jpg|thumb|The [[AEV 3 Kodiak]] has an articulated excavator arm and bulldozer blade among its adaptations for obstruction removal.]] The [[AEV 3 Kodiak]] is a [[combat engineering vehicle]] conversion of the Leopard 2 used by Germany, the Netherlands, Singapore, Sweden, and Switzerland. It is equipped with a bulldozer blade, [[excavator]] arm, and dual capstan winches. In lieu of a turret, a [[Remote Weapon Station]] or other armaments can be fitted. It is built on the Leopard 2 chassis with a built-up forward superstructure. The vehicle is used primarily for the clearance of obstacles, including minefields. The Dutch version has additional bomblet protection for the crew compartments. Spain may procure 24 examples for the Spanish Army from converted Leopard 2A4 hulls (one vehicle has been trialled in Spain)''Ejercito De Tierra'', p. 58, Antonio J. Candil Muñoz, Tankograd Publishing, 2010. and the type will be offered to Germany.{{citation needed|date=March 2020}} ==== Panzerschnellbrücke 2 ==== {{Main|{{ill|Panzerschnellbrücke 2|lt=Panzerschnellbrücke 2|de|Panzerschnellbrücke 2}}}} This vehicle, created by [[MAN SE|MAN Mobile Bridges GmbH]], is an [[armoured vehicle-launched bridge]] developed from the Leopard 2 tank chassis. It is designed to carry a folding mobile bridge, which it can "launch" across a river. Once emplaced, the bridge is sturdy enough to support most vehicles, even other Leopard tanks. When the crossing is complete, the bridge layer simply hooks up to the bridge and re-stows it.{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} [[File:Panzerschnellbrücke Leguan.jpg|thumb|A Panzerschnellbrücke Leguan folding mobile bridge on a Leopard 2 chassis, demonstrated by the German Army]] ==== Panzerschnellbrücke Leguan ==== {{Main|{{ill|Leguan bridgelayer|de|Panzerschnellbrücke Leguan}}}} This modular system combines a bridge module created by MAN Mobile Bridges GmbH with a tank chassis. The Bundeswehr is testing the {{ill|Leguan bridgelayer|de|Panzerschnellbrücke Leguan|vertical-align=sup}} on a Leopard 2 chassis.{{cite press release|url=http://www.baainbw.de/portal/a/baain/start/aktuell/allena/!ut/p/z1/hY_RC4IwEMb_I29ONHtULBNERcNyLzF02MI2GUt66I9vI-pNuocP7vvufscBgTMQQRc-Us2loJPpOxJc4jA_5niLcVLtMMq8Q-vXcYnKFEMLp38jxMRopSIEDRPQGcZmneFBAwTIwJxeCqataiY0NzoqqqVyZqn0ZJOHUiZx-AAdcpMYYe97yn1FVbBrUuwFSRbXFnijC33-dmlvn4buSsUwsUr20ceY7_uwKPzxDdw28pM!|title=Prototype of the LEGUAN Assault Bridge Arrives as Scheduled|publisher=BAAINBw|date=2017-07-06|access-date=2017-07-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180722184749/http://www.baainbw.de/portal/a/baain/start/aktuell/allena/!ut/p/z1/hY_RC4IwEMb_I29ONHtULBNERcNyLzF02MI2GUt66I9vI-pNuocP7vvufscBgTMQQRc-Us2loJPpOxJc4jA_5niLcVLtMMq8Q-vXcYnKFEMLp38jxMRopSIEDRPQGcZmneFBAwTIwJxeCqataiY0NzoqqqVyZqn0ZJOHUiZx-AAdcpMYYe97yn1FVbBrUuwFSRbXFnijC33-dmlvn4buSsUwsUr20ceY7_uwKPzxDdw28pM!|archive-date=2018-07-22|url-status=dead}} ==== Driver Training Tank ==== The Leopard 2 Driver Training Tank, as the name implies, is a non-combatant Leopard 2 for instructing soldiers in the finer points of handling the tank. The turret is supplanted by a weighted and fixed observation cab with forward and side-facing windows and a dummy gun. The instructor rides in this cab, with override controls for critical systems, and space is provided for two other students to observe.{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} ==== Leopard 2R ==== A heavy breaching and de-mining vehicle developed by [[Patria (company)|Patria]] for the Finnish Army, based on the Leopard 2A4. Six vehicles were converted. The vehicles are equipped with a mine plough or a dozer blade, and an automated marking system.{{cite web|url=http://www.janes.com/extract/jdw2007/jdw34244.html|title=Finland improves mobility systems|access-date=2009-01-08|date=2007-10-01|publisher=[[Jane's Defence Weekly]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080915061230/http://www.janes.com/extract/jdw2007/jdw34244.html|archive-date=2008-09-15}}{{cite web|url=http://www.janes.com/extracts/extract/jmvl/jmvla084.html|title=Patria Land & Armament Heavy Mine Breaching Vehicle (Finland)|access-date=2009-01-17|date=2009-01-09|publisher=[[Jane's]] Military Vehicles and Logistics}} {{dead link|fix-attempted=yes|date=June 2016|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} All were donated to Ukraine in 2023. ==== Leopard 2L ==== An armoured vehicle-launched bridge developed by KMW and Patria for the Finnish Army. Niemcy torpedują doktrynę Merkel – Defence24|date=2015-03-26}} In 2016, the Saudi Arabian ambassador to Germany stated that Saudi Arabia was no longer interested in purchasing Leopard tanks and suggested that the issue was being exploited for internal political gain.{{cite web|title=السعودية "غير" مهتمة بشراء دبابات ليوبارد الألمانية {{!}} DW {{!}} 31 May 2016|url=https://www.dw.com/ar/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%AF%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%BA%D9%8A%D8%B1-%D9%85%D9%87%D8%AA%D9%85%D8%A9-%D8%A8%D8%B4%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D8%AF%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D9%84%D9%8A%D9%88%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D9%84%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%8A%D8%A9/a-19295253|trans-title=Saudi Arabia is "not" interested in buying German Leopard tanks|access-date=2023-04-12|website=DW.COM|language=ar-AE}}{{cite news|title=Rüstungsexporte aus Deutschland: Saudi-Arabien will keine Leopard-Panzer mehr|last=Hans|first=Hans|date=2016-05-31|language=de-DE|work=Tagesspiegel Online|url=https://www.tagesspiegel.de/politik/saudi-arabien-will-keine-leopard-panzer-mehr-3726445.html|access-date=2023-04-12|issn=1865-2263}} ; {{flag|Slovenia}} : The [[Government of Slovenia|Slovenian government]] had announced its intention to send its tank fleet of old Yugoslav M-84 and [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] [[T-72]] tanks to Ukraine in exchange for German Leopard 2 tanks and Marder Infantry Fighting Vehicles in 2022.{{cite web|title=Slovenia Sending Tanks to Ukraine in Weapons Swap with Germany|url=https://www.total-slovenia-news.com/politics/9907-slovenia-sending-tanks-to-ukraine-in-weapons-swap-with-germany|access-date=2023-10-18|website=www.total-slovenia-news.com|language=en-gb}}{{cite web|date=2022-09-20|title=Germany, Slovenia want to speed up supply of tanks to Ukraine|url=https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-defense/3527430-germany-slovenia-want-to-speed-up-supply-of-tanks-to-ukraine.html|access-date=2023-10-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920173140/https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-defense/3527430-germany-slovenia-want-to-speed-up-supply-of-tanks-to-ukraine.html|archive-date=2022-09-20|url-status=live}} But Slovenia then provided Ukraine with only older [[T-54/T-55|T-55]] Soviet tanks prompting Germany to withhold its promised Leopard 2 tanks and giving only Marder Infantry Fighting Vehicles to Slovenia.{{cite web|date=2023-01-16|title=300 tanks for Ukraine: who could give it the gear to beat Russia|url=https://euromaidanpress.com/2023/01/16/where-can-ukraine-get-battle-tanks-to-mount-counteroffensive/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Euromaidan Press|language=en-US}}{{cite web|title=Slovenia to provide its fleet of M-84 main battle tanks to Ukraine|url=https://www.armyrecognition.com/defense_news_april_2022_global_security_army_industry/slovenia_to_provide_its_fleet_of_m-84_main_battle_tanks_to_ukraine.html|access-date=2023-10-18|website=www.armyrecognition.com|date=2022-04-21}} ; The Leopard 2 is a third generation German main battle tank (MBT). Developed by Krauss-Maffei in the 1970s, the tank entered service in 1979 and replaced the earlier Leopard 1 as the main battle tank of the West German army. Various iterations of the Leopard 2 continue to be operated by the armed forces of Germany, as well as 13 other European countries, and several non-European countries, including Canada, Chile, Indonesia, and Singapore. Some operating countries have licensed the Leopard 2 design for local production and domestic development.
There are two main development tranches of the Leopard 2. The first encompasses tanks produced up to the Leopard 2A4 standard and are characterised by their vertically faced turret armour. The second tranche, from Leopard 2A5 onwards, has an angled, arrow-shaped, turret appliqué armour, together with other improvements. The main armament of all Leopard 2 tanks is a smoothbore 120 mm cannon made by Rheinmetall. This is operated with a digital fire control system, laser rangefinder, and advanced night vision and sighting equipment. The tank is powered by a V12 twin-turbo diesel engine made by MTU Friedrichshafen.
In the 1990s, the Leopard 2 was used by the German Army on peacekeeping operations in Kosovo. In the 2000s, Dutch, Danish and Canadian forces deployed their Leopard 2 tanks in the War in Afghanistan as part of their contribution to the International Security Assistance Force. In the 2010s, Turkish Leopard 2 tanks saw action in Syria. Since 2023, Ukrainian Leopard 2 tanks are seeing action in the Russo-Ukrainian War.
